16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T6a1,The public material does not expose enough technical detail to support strong claims about the underlying method. A few points are explicit.

1. The model exposes effort settings. Users can trade off intelligence against speed and token cost. This strongly suggests productized test-time compute, with a smoother performance-cost frontier across different inference budgets.

2. The model is described as more proactive and better at verification and iterative refinement. The examples are telling: writing its own computer-vision pipeline, building a test harness when no live validation source exists, and fixing root causes rather than surface symptoms. These behaviors usually come from tool-use training, long-horizon task optimization, and reward shaping around task completion rather than answer generation.

3. Safety appears to combine model behavior with external classifiers and routing logic. The post mentions cyber classifiers, flagged-request fallback, and a Cyber Verification Program with reduced restrictions. That points to deployment-time capability gating rather than relying only on refusal behavior inside the base model.

4. Platform updates such as mid-conversation tool changes and automatic fallbacks indicate that Anthropic is designing around agentic workflows as a first-class use case. This is not an architectural innovation in the model itself, but it does reflect where the training and product stack are being optimized.

From a research perspective, the most plausible technical center of gravity is high-quality post-training, test-time compute control, tool-interaction training, and safety-classifier coordination, not a newly disclosed pretraining paradigm.18:T79c,The post reports benchmark outcomes and anecdotal case studies, but it does not provide enough protocol detail, confidence intervals, or training/inference budget disclosure for rigorous scientific interpretation.

Still, several quantitative claims are explicit:
- On Frontier-Bench v0.1, Opus 5 surpasses other models and more than doubles Opus 4.8’s performance at lower cost per task.
- On CursorBench 3.2, at max effort it is within 0.5% of Fable 5’s peak score at roughly half the cost per task; at high, xhigh, and max effort it offers better performance at a given cost than competing models.
- On ARC-AGI 3, its score is reported as roughly 3x the next-best model.
- On Zapier AutomationBench, its pass rate is about 1.5x the next-best model at the same cost per task, and even the lowest effort setting beats other models.
- On OSWorld 2.0, it outperforms other models at any given cost and exceeds Fable 5’s best result at a little over one-third of the cost.
- On internal life-sciences evaluations, it improves over Opus 4.8 across the board, including +10.2 points on an organic chemistry benchmark and +7.7 points on protein variant function prediction.

The safety section also contains useful signals:
- Anthropic describes Opus 5 as its most aligned model so far in automated behavioral audits, with lower deceptive behavior and lower susceptibility to misuse.
- Despite intentionally avoiding cyber-task training, the model has improved substantially on cyber evaluations through general capability gains.
- It is close to Mythos 5 on vulnerability finding but remains substantially behind on exploit development.
- Cyber classifiers are expected to intervene about 85% less often than for Fable 5.

The main takeaway is that Anthropic is pushing hard on the cost-performance frontier, while also confirming that general capability improvements can raise sensitive capabilities even without direct domain-specific training.19:T4bb,This is best read selectively in 15–20 minutes. Start with the benchmark section and only retain claims with explicit relative numbers. Ignore the launch language. Then read the case studies, not for the stories themselves, but for the behavioral pattern: does the model build tools, verify its own work, and search for root causes rather than patching symptoms? Finally, read the safety section carefully, especially the points that cyber capability improved without explicit cyber training and that flagged requests can be routed through classifier-based fallback.

For a pretraining researcher, three questions are worth carrying forward:
- What kind of test-time compute control sits behind the effort settings, and was the model trained to support multiple inference budgets?
- How much of the observed agentic behavior comes from pretraining versus post-training?
- Why do general capability gains appear to improve vulnerability discovery more readily than exploit generation when explicit cyber training is absent?

It is not a good idea to treat the benchmark rankings here as strict scientific conclusions, because the post lacks the protocol detail and training disclosure needed for that standard.1a:T4bc,The post is a position statement rather than a technical contribution, but its policy ranking is precise. First, restrict access to advanced chips and chipmaking equipment for authoritarian states, and crack down on smuggling and evasion, because scaling laws imply that without sufficient chips it is not possible to train models beyond the U.S. frontier. Second, target industrial-scale distillation, because distillation is far more compute-efficient than training from scratch and can compress the capability gap to a few months even under chip constraints; in the author's view, this matters much more than whether weights are open or closed. Third, require mandatory pre-release safety testing for all sufficiently capable models, open or closed, regardless of origin, with emphasis on cyber, biological, and alignment risks. The author argues that banning U.S. companies from using Chinese open weights does not address misuse, because malicious actors are unlikely to be regulated U.S. businesses. Open weights do introduce unique safety problems—weak guardrail enforcement, limited monitoring, and irreversible release—but the proposed response is capability-based testing rather than a blanket ban.1b:T414,The analysis incorporates normalization-induced scale invariance into loss-landscape stability. For weights feeding into normalization layers such as BN or LN, rescaling the weight vector may leave the network function largely unchanged. The loss is therefore insensitive to radial scaling, but the curvature is not. When the norm of such a weight block becomes small, the relevant Hessian eigenvalues can be amplified, roughly following the inverse scale of the norm. Weight decay supplies a persistent shrinkage force, so increasing the decay coefficient drives these blocks toward a high-sharpness region. The paper then defines a weight-norm criticality indicator combining local Hessian information and the learning rate. A practical feature is the component-wise decomposition: one can evaluate the restricted Hessian for a specific scale-invariant block instead of the full parameter Hessian. This makes the criterion applicable to architectures with many normalization modules and allows attribution of instability to individual layers.1c:T5b8,OPTScientist is a theory-guided multi-agent framework built on three core layers: 1) A typed domain-specific language (DSL) that decomposes optimizer updates into six reusable modules — direction, scaling, preconditioning, regularization, state, and parameter grouping — instead of generating arbitrary Python code. A companion compiler validates tensor/scalar compatibility before training, lowers candidates into an intermediate representation, and produces executable optimizers to filter invalid proposals early. 2) A scientific search loop coordinating four specialized roles in a single orchestration cycle: Theorist (proposes hypotheses and priors from shared memory), Designer (synthesizes diverse DSL candidates), Engineer (compiles, repairs, and evaluates candidates), and Reviewer (scores candidates along novelty, validity, performance, target-stage behavior, and scalability axes). 3) Two-stage evolution: Stage one runs evolutionary search over optimizer programs within the current DSL; stage two proposes conservative DSL extensions (e.g., safe macro-like composition primitives) when repeated failures, performance plateaus, or compiler bottlenecks reveal representational limitations, enabling adaptive expansion of the search space. The discovered RS-MR optimizer combines row-normalized polar directions, lightweight global damping, and soft blockwise update gating, improving matrix update selectivity using only compact block-level state.1d:T679,The system is built as a five-stage adaptation pipeline. The base is Italia 10B, a from-scratch dense decoder-only Transformer trained on about 9T tokens across 50+ languages, with a native 16K context. Architecturally it is fairly standard for its size: 40 layers, hidden size 4096, GQA with 48 query heads and 8 KV heads, RoPE, squared ReLU MLPs, no dropout, and untied embeddings. Stage 1 is continued pretraining to extend the native context from 16,384 to 32,768 tokens, with the RoPE base reset to 500,000 at that boundary. This is not just positional extrapolation; it is meant to let the model adapt its attention behavior under a new length distribution. At inference time, YaRN is then used to stretch the context further to 131,072 tokens. Stage 2 is large-scale SFT on a 12.3B-token instruction mixture, followed by a short math-focused annealing run before RL. That annealing step is important: it narrows the policy toward verifiable reasoning before entering a higher-variance RL phase. Stage 3 applies GRPO with verifiable rewards, initially on math. Stage 4 inserts DPO under what the paper calls the Delta Learning Hypothesis, suggesting DPO is used as a preference-boundary correction step rather than as a replacement for RL. Stage 5 runs multi-environment GRPO over five domains: mathematics, code, multiple-choice QA, instruction following, and tool calling. The intent is to avoid over-specializing the policy to a single reward shape. The model is also exposed in dual inference modes, thinking on and thinking off, indicating that the chat template and decoding interface were designed with explicit reasoning-token control in mind.1e:T4dd,The empirical section is relatively restrained, which makes it more useful. Domyn-Small is compared against Qwen3.5-9B, OLMo-3-7B-Think, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-8B-v1, and Ministral-3-8B-Reasoning-2512. The headline result is not absolute accuracy leadership but an accuracy-efficiency balance: on reasoning benchmarks, Domyn-Small reportedly uses about one-third as many output tokens per problem as Qwen3.5-9B on average, which matters directly for serving cost. In accuracy terms, it outperforms Nemotron-Nano and Ministral on instruction following and GPQA-Diamond, is roughly on par with Ministral on AIME 2025, and trails Qwen3.5-9B and OLMo-3-7B-Think by a clear margin on hard math reasoning. The paper attributes that gap to two factors: the RL phase had not fully converged at the checkpoint used for evaluation, and the base model predates the recent wave of reasoning-oriented pretraining practices. That explanation is plausible and also useful, because it prevents over-reading post-training gains as if they were unconstrained. On context length, the setup is also informative: 32K native context after CPT, then 128K-class inference via YaRN. This is a pragmatic compromise rather than full native ultra-long-context pretraining.1f:T5d2,The method is Pipelined Gradient Coding (PGC). Standard gradient coding assigns each worker c=s+1 data partitions and asks it to compute all c gradients in the same step, then upload a coded linear combination. PGC spreads those c computations across multiple consecutive steps, so each worker computes only one partition gradient per step, matching the per-step compute cost of ordinary distributed gradient descent.

To preserve recoverability, the coded message at a given step is formed from gradients computed at the current and previous steps. This creates a temporal pipeline: redundancy is no longer concentrated within one step, but distributed over time.

The paper develops PGC for two classic placement schemes:
1. Fractional Repetition (FR): workers are grouped and share the same partition placement. PGC-FR is simpler to encode and decode.
2. Cyclic Repetition (CR): partitions are placed cyclically, which is more flexible and does not require c to divide n, but decoding is more involved and depends on the straggler pattern.

The main technical shift is from purely spatial redundancy to spatial-plus-temporal redundancy. This introduces delayed gradients, so the paper also provides convergence analysis under smooth and strongly convex settings. In other words, PGC trades extra same-step computation for analyzable gradient staleness. Compared with asynchronous SGD, the delay here is structured by coding rather than being an uncontrolled side effect of worker timing.20:T43c,The experiments first validate the motivation. On 12 Google Cloud VMs, training ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 for one epoch, the authors compare vanilla distributed gradient descent with GC under FR and CR placement. All methods follow the same loss-per-step trajectory because they recover the same full gradient, but GC is consistently slower per step. The paper states that the slowdown relative to DGD exceeds 100%, and the gap widens as the tolerated straggler count s increases. GC-FR is faster than GC-CR due to lower coding complexity.

The second part evaluates PGC through simulations and real experiments. The main result is that PGC substantially reduces completion time relative to standard GC and improves convergence in wall-clock time, while keeping per-step compute close to DGD. The important nuance is that the gain is primarily in time-to-train, not necessarily in steps-to-convergence, since PGC uses delayed gradients. The method is most attractive when stragglers are present but not catastrophic, and when the compute amplification of standard GC is the dominant cost.21:T414,A skim read should take about 20–30 minutes. Start with the introduction and preliminary section to understand why the authors think classic GC is often a poor systems trade-off. Then look closely at Fig. 3; it captures the paper’s motivation well: same recovered gradient, much worse step time.

Next, read the construction of PGC for FR and CR. If time is limited, focus on the FR version first because it is easier to internalize. The key idea to retain is simple: one partition per worker per step, but coded recovery across multiple steps. After that, scan the convergence section to see how pipeline delay is handled, and then the experiments to check whether the benefit appears in step efficiency or wall-clock efficiency.

Two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: how this kind of temporal coding would interact with gradient accumulation, pipeline parallelism, or elastic training in LLM pretraining; and whether delayed coded gradients behave differently under adaptive optimizers such as AdamW compared with plain SGD.22:T965,技术路线很扎实，核心在于把“局部近似是否有效”做成可直接检验的实验。模型是 150M 参数 Transformer，在 FineWeb 上训练 3B tokens，并每 10% 训练进度保存 checkpoint。围绕每个 checkpoint，作者构造两类代理目标。prox 是对网络输出做一阶线性化，但保留交叉熵，因此等价于 NTK 参数化下的多类 logistic regression；quad 则进一步把这个目标在 checkpoint 处做二阶展开，得到凸二次目标。然后从同一个 checkpoint 出发，在相同数据流和训练设置下继续训练这些代理模型，并与原始非线性模型的真实轨迹比较。这里关键不是只比较 loss 数值，而是比较在一个非平凡时间窗口内，代理模型是否能复现真实训练的下降趋势和超参敏感性。

在谱分析部分，作者估计 Hessian 和 Gauss-Newton 矩阵的谱，并分别考察原始参数空间和 Adam 预条件后的谱。方法上使用很深的 Lanczos quadrature probe，并给出误差带，分辨率覆盖约六个数量级。这一点很重要，因为很多过去的谱结论只看头部几个特征值，难以判断尾部是否真有稳定幂律。作者发现谱存在清晰的 head-tail 分裂：head 的大小与 vocab size 对齐，且主要来自 unembedding；tail 呈 power law，并且在不同 batch size 下几乎重合，Adam 预条件也不改变其形状，只改变某些尺度关系。基于这些谱，作者进一步估计 source exponent β 和 capacity exponent α，在可分辨尾部中得到 α≈1，而 β<1，不满足一些文献常用的可求和假设。这意味着若用经典 inverse-problem 或 kernel-regression 风格的谱假设来分析 LLM 训练，很多前提并不成立。

稳定性分析则把理论预测和真实 blow-up 实验对上。作者从多个 checkpoint 出发，用预条件 SGD 在学习率和 batch size 的乘子网格上做扫描，直接测哪些组合会发散，再与线性稳定性分析给出的边界比较。这里的“预条件 SGD”是为了更贴近 Adam 类训练的局部线性动力学。结果显示，小中 batch 下，噪声会把系统推到 stochastic edge-of-stability；大 batch 下则更接近经典线性理论中的 deterministic edge。这个设计的好处是，它没有把 edge-of-stability 当作单一现象，而是区分了噪声主导和曲率主导两种机制。23:T500,The contribution is important less as a new optimizer and more as a validation layer for a large body of optimization reasoning. First, it shows that local Taylor proxies are not merely infinitesimal approximations: in a 150M-parameter transformer trained on 3B tokens, they can remain predictive over windows as long as roughly 10% of total training, with noticeably better agreement later in training. That gives empirical support to using quadratic analyses for practical pretraining questions. Second, the spectral measurements are unusually informative: the spectrum separates into a head whose size is set by vocabulary and dominated by the unembedding layer, and a power-law tail that is nearly invariant across batch sizes and largely unaffected by Adam preconditioning. That is directly relevant to output-layer parameterization, tokenizer/vocabulary choices, and curvature structure. Third, the stability analysis sharpens the edge-of-stability story: small and medium batches operate in a noise-dominated stochastic edge regime, while large batches move toward the deterministic edge predicted by linear theory. The broader implication is that LLM training is typically run close to stability limits regardless of batch size, but the mechanism changes with noise scale.24:T9e0,The methodology is strong because the paper turns a vague theoretical claim into a falsifiable training experiment. The base model is a 150M transformer trained on 3B FineWeb tokens, with checkpoints saved every 10% of training. Around each checkpoint, the authors build two local proxies. The first, prox, linearizes the network outputs while keeping the cross-entropy objective; this is equivalent to multiclass logistic regression in the NTK parameterization. The second, quad, further takes a second-order Taylor expansion of that objective, yielding a convex quadratic problem. Starting from the same checkpoint, they continue training these proxy systems and compare them against the original nonlinear trajectory under matched conditions. The key point is not just local loss fitting at a single step, but whether the proxies reproduce meaningful optimization behavior over a sizable future window.

For geometry, the paper estimates Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra along training, both before and after Adam-style preconditioning. The estimation uses very deep Lanczos quadrature probes with error bands, resolving the spectrum over roughly six orders of magnitude. This is a major practical detail: many prior empirical studies only resolve the top few eigenvalues, which is insufficient for claims about tail behavior. The resulting picture is a clear head-tail split. The head is tied to vocabulary size and is dominated by the unembedding layer. The tail follows a power law and appears universal in the sense that it is nearly identical across batch sizes and not materially altered by Adam preconditioning. Using these curves, the authors estimate a capacity exponent around alpha ≈ 1 in the resolvable tail and a source exponent beta < 1, contradicting summability assumptions that appear in parts of the optimization and inverse-problems literature.

For stability, the paper combines theory with direct blow-up tests. From multiple checkpoints, it runs preconditioned SGD over a grid of learning-rate and batch-size multipliers, measuring which settings diverge and comparing the observed boundary to linear stability predictions. This is a good design choice because it tests the practical content of edge-of-stability theory rather than treating it as a metaphor. The results separate two regimes: stochastic edge of stability at small to medium batch sizes, where gradient noise is essential, and deterministic edge of stability at large batch sizes, where classical linear analysis becomes more accurate.25:T7ee,The main experiments use a 150M-parameter transformer trained on 3B FineWeb tokens. Checkpoints are saved every 10% of training, and around each checkpoint the authors construct the prox and quad local surrogates. The central empirical result is that both surrogates can track the real optimization trajectory over windows up to about 10% of total training, with substantially better agreement later in training than early on. The paper does not claim that a single quadratic model explains the entire run; the claim is more precise and more useful: over a practically meaningful local horizon, the approximation is predictive enough to support analysis.

The spectral experiments estimate Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra with deep Lanczos probes over six orders of magnitude. Three observations stand out. First, the spectral head has a size linked to vocabulary and is dominated by the unembedding layer, indicating that the output layer contributes a distinct curvature structure. Second, the tail follows a stable power law and is almost unchanged across batch sizes. Third, Adam preconditioning does not remove this tail structure, suggesting that preconditioning does not whiten the problem into something close to isotropic geometry. From the measured spectra, the paper estimates a capacity exponent alpha ≈ 1 and a source exponent beta < 1 in the resolvable tail, which runs against common summability assumptions.

The stability experiments scan learning-rate and batch-size multipliers to map divergence boundaries. The outcome is that training spends most of its time near the edge of stability. At small and medium batch sizes, the regime is noise-dominated and better described as a stochastic edge of stability. At large batch sizes, the observed boundary aligns more closely with deterministic linear stability theory. The predictive quality of the linearized analysis also improves later in training, matching the earlier observation that local Taylor models become more accurate toward the end of pretraining.26:T6f2,A good reading order is: first verify that the local approximation is genuinely predictive, then study the spectral structure, then read the stability section.

Start with the introduction and the main experiments in Section 3. Focus on how prox and quad are defined, how the checkpoint-based continuation experiments are set up, and what exactly it means for a proxy to remain predictive over a 10%-of-training window. That section determines whether the rest of the paper should be taken as more than a theoretical analogy.

Then read Section 4 carefully. The most important figures are the Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra, the before/after-Adam comparisons, and the evidence for the head-tail split. Two questions are worth keeping in mind. Why is the spectral head so tightly linked to vocabulary size and the unembedding layer? And why is the power-law tail so insensitive to batch size and Adam preconditioning? Those observations have implications for output-layer design, tokenizer/vocabulary choices, and what parts of optimization geometry are intrinsic versus optimizer-induced.

Finally, read Section 5 on stability. Pay attention to how blow-up is operationally defined, how the learning-rate/batch-size multiplier grid is constructed, and how the measured instability boundary compares to linear predictions. The distinction between stochastic and deterministic edge-of-stability regimes is the part most likely to matter for practical pretraining recipes, especially for batch scaling and schedule design.

A full careful read likely takes 1.5 to 2.5 hours because this is a large-stack technical report rather than a narrow method paper.2b:T44b,The architecture repeatedly applies one Transformer block Fθ to a hidden state, h^{t+1}=Fθ(h^t,e), with optional input injection through a learned adapter. The main grid uses NoPE, with positional-encoding controls in the appendix. The key methodological move is to replace tail instruments with a head instrument. Tail instruments such as skipping a late loop or comparing Jacobians across late loops are unreliable because converged trajectories sit near fixed points; near such states, skipping is cheap and local circuits look similar by construction. The proposed diagnostic is convergence-time scaling τ(n,i): the first loop at which the decoded output at position i reaches its final value and stays there. Its scaling class acts as a mechanism signature. Constant τ indicates shortcut or refinement, τ proportional to log n indicates a parallel scan, and τ proportional to n indicates serial step-indexed computation. A streaming positive control validates the instrument: when token i is revealed only at loop i, τ recovers a linear slope of 1.0, while shortcut controls remain flat.2c:T577,The experiments are controlled population studies over many seeds, recipes, and model sizes. The reported scales include a small model with a 2-layer block and d=128, a medium model with a 2-layer block and d=256, and a larger model with a 4-layer block and d=512. Tasks include prefix parity, LSB-first increment-with-carry, and group word problems over Z60, S4, S5, and A5. These tasks have known algorithmic structure: some admit constant-depth shortcuts, while S5 and A5 connect to NC1-complete word problems, and associative scan gives a logarithmic-depth solution in principle. The main empirical result is a linear computation frontier learned by free training. The frontier solves v positions per loop, with v approximately n_tr/T_tr; under T=n training, the speed is about 1 position per loop. Giving more loops at test time rescues late positions at fixed input length. Standard tail diagnostics fail: skip retention is essentially total on sufficiently solved examples, cross-step Jacobian alignment is uniformly high, and these metrics do not predict length generalization. The study also separates optimization walls from circuit complexity: A5 hardness is not the main barrier, while S5 operator scale is; an operator-first curriculum removes that wall. Budget annealing transfers the learned mechanism across loop contracts in 4 out of 4 seeds, avoiding the from-scratch seed lottery.2d:T655,The study pretrains 48 models across 160M-class and 410M-class settings, using 2B FineWeb-Edu tokens per run. At 160M, six standard RoPE seeds show a severe seed lottery: NIAH accuracy at length 512 ranges from 14% to 98%, while perplexity gives little warning. Across the 12 RoPE-vs-hybrid models, the correlation between perplexity and retrieval is only +0.206. The hybrid Möbius arm keeps perplexity essentially unchanged, 29.66 versus 29.72 for standard RoPE, but reaches 90.3±5.7% NIAH accuracy at length 512 and greatly reduces seed variance. The raw variance ratio at L=512 is about 30.8×, robust variance tests give p=0.013–0.029, and the worst seed improves from 14% to 86%. With f_n → 1 the model achieves near-identity retention without shrinking the write magnitude; with f_n → 0 and i_n → 1 it decisively overwrites stale state; with both gates large it preserves old state while writing new information. The recurrence remains diagonal, input-dependent, and parallel-scan compatible, retaining Mamba-style linear-time efficiency. In a pure-uniform SEDD checkpoint, 6.69% of 3.29 billion audited candidate scores violate the coordinate box. During generation with the released SEDD sampler on 128 sequences, 25.02% of complete score vectors contain a coordinate violation, and another 56.23% pass all coordinate bounds but are still incompatible with any valid clean-token posterior. The sampler encounters negative pre-normalization weights in these cases and effectively samples from their positive part. The theory also shows that the conditional score-entropy risk is uniquely minimized at the true score and gives a rank condition under which the posterior is uniquely recoverable; pure-uniform corruption satisfies it.30:T4f7,FlowEdit is a training framework centered on information-theoretic dual-objective control of reasoning flows: 1) It maps each reasoning branch to a designated hidden state along the generation trajectory as the flow representation, converting the abstract requirement of maintaining multiple parallel reasoning flows into concrete geometric constraints on these hidden representations. 2) It constructs a pair of dual objectives based on conditional mutual information: maximize the information flow from each selected hypothesis to its branch outcome (ensuring each branch retains sufficient information to independently derive its conclusion); minimize conditional overlap across sibling branches given the preceding autoregressive context (eliminating inter-branch redundancy and guaranteeing diversity). 3) It selects the shared analysis embedding (rather than only the prompt embedding) as the conditioning variable under an ε-sufficiency condition, which provably isolates the residual redundancy to be penalized while preserving the common problem structure that distinct branches are entitled to encode. 4) The objectives are optimized via tractable variational bounds combined with boundary embeddings, requiring no modifications to the base model architecture.31:T577,The method, Byte-Prefix Marginalization, rewrites the teacher’s next-token distribution in the student vocabulary through a shared byte representation. For each teacher token, BPM takes its byte string and finds the longest student token whose byte string is a prefix of that teacher token’s bytes. The teacher token’s probability is assigned to that student token, and probabilities mapped to the same student token are aggregated. Probability mass that cannot be matched is assigned to an explicit residual category, which is required to preserve total mass. When byte prefixes do not span multiple teacher tokens, the transformed target exactly recovers the teacher’s byte-prefix marginal. At spanning positions, the method uses a mass-preserving chain-factorized lower bound. Training remains on-policy: the student generates trajectories, the teacher is queried at the corresponding byte-aligned states, and the student minimizes a generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence to the transformed target. Compared with candidate-set methods such as SimCT, BPM avoids dropping mass; compared with rank-based methods such as ULD or GOLD, it avoids assigning probability to byte-unrelated student tokens; compared with SeqKD, it keeps dense next-token supervision. A precomputed mask removes all-whitespace target positions in code data to prevent learning tokenizer-specific formatting artifacts.32:T449,Multi-Block Editing adds a bounded revision phase to block diffusion. At inference time, after a new block is decoded, the method reopens a sliding window of already decoded blocks and performs joint forward passes over that window, allowing earlier tokens to be revised using later context. The design avoids token-level rollback logic and keeps the computation bounded by editing whole blocks through direct token-to-token revision. For windows beyond adjacent blocks, an entropy-based historical surprisal watermark is used to select the previously decoded block that is most likely to contain errors, rather than recomputing all history. The training component, Multi-Block Edit SFT, introduces bidirectional attention masks and a curriculum that expands the edit span from 2 to 4 blocks, so the model learns to exploit multi-block context instead of seeing it only at inference time. On the systems side, the authors extend SGLang with a multi-shape CUDA Graph pool and fine-grained KV-cache control to support interleaved single-block decoding and variable-length multi-block editing passes.33:T517,The work first proposes Routing Slot Memories (RSM), a unifying framework that decomposes fixed-size memory updates into two independent dimensions: (1) write routing, which selects a subset of memory slots to write new content to; (2) slot-wise decay, which applies forgetting operators only to slots that receive new writes, leaving unselected slots completely untouched with no overwrites or decay. Under this framework, SSMs correspond to the extreme of dense full-slot writes with global gradual decay, while SWA corresponds to the extreme of deterministic round-robin single-slot writes with hard eviction (unselected slots retain content until overwritten on their rotation). Raven is a concrete RSM instantiation that uses learned, input-dependent sparse routing to select a small subset of slots per step—neither writing to all slots nor rotating deterministically through a single slot. New content is only written to selected slots, and learnable decay is applied exclusively to these updated slots, while unselected slots retain their content indefinitely without any update or decay. The Raven block requires no auxiliary convolution or sliding-window attention layers; a single RSM layer supports both persistent memory and precise recall while maintaining strict linear time complexity.34:T5ea,Two complementary solutions are proposed, each sidestepping positional uncertainty through a distinct mechanism and producing a different form of any-order inference:
1. Insertion-based masked diffusion (FlexMDM): Adds token insertion capability to standard MDMs, breaking the fixed-canvas constraint. Tokens are no longer committed to a fixed final position during unmasking, as later insertions can shift existing tokens, reducing the positional commitment burden. This approach yields structural any-order inference: generation alternates across different nodes of the parsed program tree, rather than completing one contiguous region at a time. It is implemented by fine-tuning Dream-Coder 7B, a general-purpose code generation MDM, to support insertion operations.
2. Latent-space masked diffusion (LatentMDM): The core modeling contribution. It moves masked diffusion from discrete token space to a continuous latent space, shifting decision granularity from individual token positions to masked latent segments, elevating the prediction interface to a coarser semantic granularity and eliminating token-level positional uncertainty at the root. This approach yields semantic any-order inference: the model searches over semantic generation orders in latent space, completely unconstrained by left-to-right token order. Unlike prior embedding-space diffusion methods (e.g., DUO, 𝕊-FLM), LatentMDM does not predict around individual token positions, but directly operates on semantic-level latent segments.35:T520,Experiments are conducted in two scales and domains:
1. 7B parameter code generation: FlexMDM is fine-tuned from Dream-Coder 7B, evaluated on four benchmarks: HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, and MBPP+. Results show FlexMDM outperforms the base Dream-Coder 7B on Pass@16 for HumanEval and HumanEval+, and leads on Pass@1 for MBPP and MBPP+, with overall on-par performance. Qualitative analysis confirms FlexMDM exhibits genuine structural any-order generation (jumping across AST nodes), while standard MDM with confidence decoding produces outputs nearly identical to strict left-to-right decoding.
2. 125M parameter math reasoning: LatentMDM is pretrained from scratch on TinyGSM, compared against baselines including standard MDMs, embedding-space methods (DUO, 𝕊-FLM), and an autoregressive model with KV caching. Under matched inference budgets, LatentMDM outperforms all baselines.

Directions for further exploration: Whether positional uncertainty exists in all fixed-canvas non-AR models; how latent space granularity trades off between any-order capability and generation performance; what other tasks beyond code generation can benefit from genuine any-order inference.37:T6bd,1) Definitions:
- Native Memory State: a stateful backbone whose internal dynamic parameters/state persist across multiple inferences; the state’s semantic space is aligned during pretraining or mid-training.
- Native Memory Procedure: memory operations (store/forget/update/use) are executed as part of the model computation, not via external retrieval and prompt concatenation.

2) Architecture (Metis prototype):
- Inspired by Fast Weight Programming: introduce fast-changing weights/states integrated into the backbone.
- A Metis block contains a hyper memory block and a local memory block, and injects memory via a dedicated memory-attention mechanism.
- Intuition: local memory acts like writable short-term state; hyper memory controls/stabilizes how state is written/read (akin to gating or a hypernetwork-style controller).

3) Training objectives (making memory both information-bearing and operational):
- Memory reconstruction objective: enforces that the memory state actually compresses and retains past information (an upper bound on what can be stored/recovered).
- Memory operation objectives: supervise or self-supervise the desired state transitions for write/update/forget/read, so the model learns procedures, not just storage.
- Regularization objective: improves robustness under complex scenarios, mitigating drift, contamination, or uncontrolled accumulation.

4) Data: large-scale synthetic “memory-specific” mid-training data derived from public datasets. The paper frames memory as a prediction problem under streaming constraints: you store without knowing future use, and later you can only act on what was stored, so training should force purposeful lossy compression for future utility.38:T5b9,GaugeQuant learns orthogonal rotations at transformer boundaries so that activation mass is spread more evenly across dimensions. The paper identifies usable symmetries in attention and MLP blocks. Value vectors in attention admit an SO(d_k) rotation, with corresponding transformations of W_V and W_O preserving the exact output; under GQA, each KV head group shares its rotation. Query/key rotations are constrained by RoPE: they must commute with the RoPE matrix, reducing the available symmetry to U(1)^{d_k/2}, which the paper does not exploit. In the SwiGLU MLP, the down-projection boundary also admits an invariance, but the rotation cannot be fully absorbed upstream because SiLU and the element-wise product do not commute with a general dense rotation. As a result, H·R remains a runtime operation while R^T can be fused into W_down. Instead of simulating quantization, the method adds a LogSumExp penalty on rotated boundary activations. LogSumExp acts as a smooth dense proxy for the infinity norm, which matters because the uniform quantization step size is driven by the largest outlier. A stop-gradient operator ensures that this auxiliary term updates only the rotation matrices, while the base model parameters are still trained only by cross-entropy. Compared with SpinQuant-style post-training rotation search, GaugeQuant does not require calibration data, a frozen model, or a non-differentiable quantization operator in the optimization loop.39:T6ff,方法叫 Windowed-MTP。核心思想是把 StreamingLLM 风格的 sliding window + attention sink 只应用在 draft head 上，而 target verify 仍然保留全上下文注意力。这样 draft 每一步只读取 W + sink 个 token 的 KV，而不是整段 S 长度上下文；例如 1M context 下 4K window 只占 0.4%。

为什么这能做到“lossless by construction”？因为 speculative decoding 的接受与否始终由 full-attention target 决定。windowing 只会改变 draft 提出的候选 token，不会改变 target 的验证规则，因此不会改变最终采样分布。论文还专门做了 greedy output diff，验证 windowed draft 与 native full-attention draft 的最终输出没有系统性分歧，超出范围的差异只来自 verifier 既有的 bf16 非确定性。

作者还给了一个逐步 latency model，把一次 speculative iteration 分成 γ 次 draft forward 和一次 verify forward，并分析在不同 acceptance length、draft depth d=γ+1、context length S 下，什么时候 native deep draft 会从加速退化到与 dense baseline 持平，甚至变成负收益。这个模型的意义在于，它不是只报告“快了多少”，而是解释为什么在长上下文、低 acceptance、verify 变便宜时，draft attention 会成为主导项。

机制分析部分也做得比较扎实。作者没有停留在“窗口够小也没掉速”这种经验结论，而是看了 window-size dose-response、每个 draft position 的 conditional acceptance 分解，以及 in-run decision-invariance probe。结论是：windowing 大多数时候并不改变 draft 的 top-1 proposal，保留了与 full-attention draft 相近的 acceptance profile，因此速度收益来自每步成本下降，而不是靠牺牲 acceptance 换吞吐。3a:T6a0,The method, Windowed-MTP, applies a StreamingLLM-style sliding window plus attention sink to the draft head only, while leaving the target verifier at full attention. As a result, each draft forward reads only W + sink tokens from KV instead of the full context length S. At 1M context, a 4K window is only 0.4% of the sequence.

The key point is why this remains lossless. In speculative decoding, the target verifier always decides which proposed tokens are accepted. Windowing changes only the draft proposals, not the acceptance rule. Therefore the final output distribution remains identical to standard exact speculation. The paper validates this with greedy output diffs, showing no systematic divergence beyond the verifier’s existing bf16 nondeterminism.

The authors also provide a per-step latency model. One speculative iteration is decomposed into γ draft forwards plus one verify forward, and the model explains when a deeper native draft stops helping: long context increases draft KV reads, low acceptance reduces amortization, and cheaper verify phases expose the draft cost instead of hiding it. This is useful because the paper does not merely report speedups; it explains the regime in which native MTP collapses from accelerator to liability.

The mechanistic analysis is also stronger than usual. The paper studies window-size dose response, conditional acceptance by draft position, and an in-run decision-invariance probe. The conclusion is that windowing usually preserves the draft’s top-1 proposal and closely tracks the full-attention acceptance profile. The gain therefore comes from reducing per-step draft cost, not from trading away acceptance for throughput.3b:T730,The experiments span three architecture families, including at least a dense Qwen-122B model, a hybrid Nemotron model, and a third model with a different attention design. The main operating point is 1M context with batch size 1.

First, the paper quantifies the long-context draft-attention tax. At γ=6, i.e. d=7, the draft phase alone adds about +92% to +138% on top of the bare verify cost per decode step, nearly doubling step latency. This directly falsifies the assumption that the draft is negligible at million-token context. More importantly, on hard low-acceptance workloads the shipped native draft can become net-negative: at d=7 it reaches only 0.80× the no-speculation dense baseline on Qwen-122B code QA and 0.97× on the hybrid Nemotron. Increasing draft depth to d=9 does not rescue the situation.

Windowed-MTP then delivers a fairly consistent reduction. At 1M context, it cuts per-speculative-iteration cost by about 28%–44% relative to native MTP, and the gain is largely input-invariant. Its magnitude tracks the fraction of draft cost attributable to windowable attention. The paper also measures that the draft KV pool is about 7.7%–11% of total KV across the three models; after windowing, all but W + sink of that draft KV becomes dead state and can be reclaimed into a compact ring buffer with no quality or speed penalty.

On acceptance behavior, windowing preserves the draft top-1 proposal 86%–94% of the time, and the resulting acceptance profile tracks full-attention draft within confidence intervals across the sweep. Residual differences exist, but they are small, depend on input and draft depth, and are always outweighed by the per-step latency reduction. End-to-end performance therefore never regresses in the reported settings, while exactness is preserved because the verifier is unchanged.3c:T607,This one is worth a careful read. Start with the introduction and the latency decomposition section. The central insight is not simply that acceptance matters, but that full-context draft attention becomes the dominant cost at long context, especially when the verifier has already been optimized with hybrid or linear attention. The latency model is useful because it tells you when native MTP stops being a speedup mechanism.

Then read the method section with attention to the exactness argument. The paper is careful about the distinction between approximating the proposal path and preserving the final decoding distribution through full verification. That boundary is important. After that, spend time on the acceptance analysis: the window-size sweep, per-position conditional acceptance, and decision-invariance probe explain why a relatively small local window is enough for the draft to remain a good proposer.

For experiments, prioritize the tables showing native draft becoming net-negative and the main 1M-context latency reductions. A focused read of the introduction, cost model, main experiments, and exactness validation should take about 45–60 minutes. For deeper follow-up, two questions are especially interesting: whether pretraining should explicitly encourage locality in native draft heads so they are naturally compatible with windowed inference, and whether draft and verifier attention families should be co-designed rather than attaching a full-attention MTP head to an increasingly cheap hybrid/linear verifier.3d:T5c5,The method has three layers. First, the paper analyzes non-orthogonality from both tensor approximation and dot-product error perspectives. The key point is that the error of low-rank approximation composed with quantization is not just the sum of two independent errors; cross terms appear, so the composition cannot be treated as harmless stacking. Second, it studies ordering and derives that low-rank decomposition should be applied before quantization. The intuition is sensible: if quantization is applied first, the subsequent low-rank fit is performed on an already distorted matrix, so the principal subspace estimate itself is biased by quantization noise. If low-rank decomposition comes first, the dominant structure is extracted before discretization, and the later quantization acts on a more compact and regularized representation. Third, the paper introduces DAM, a Diagonal Adhesive Method, motivated by activation outliers. After low-rank decomposition, representation statistics can shift so that a few large-magnitude channels dominate block-wise quantization scales, reducing effective resolution for the majority of values. DAM keeps a diagonal-form corrective component to preserve scale information that is poorly captured by the joint low-rank-plus-low-bit approximation. The diagonal structure is important: it adds little compute and memory overhead and can be inserted into existing pipelines without redesigning the main matrix multiplication path.3e:T492,From the provided full-text content, the experiments are organized around validating three claims rather than chasing a single best number: combined low-rank plus quantization is worse than an independence assumption would predict; low-rank-then-quantize is better than the reverse order; and DAM recovers a meaningful portion of the loss in the high-compression regime. The paper frames current empirical bottlenecks as roughly W4A4KV4 for quantization and around 50% compression ratio for low-rank decomposition, beyond which quality drops sharply. The reported experiments are designed to push beyond those bottlenecks. The excerpt does not include the full result tables, so exact benchmark deltas cannot be quoted reliably here, but the paper repeatedly claims that DAM improves compressed-model performance while preserving low cost and high speed. When reading, check whether the study spans multiple model sizes, block sizes, rank settings, and whether it quantizes only weights or also activations and KV cache. The strongest part of the paper is likely the closed loop between theory, order ablation, and outlier diagnosis, not just the final accuracy numbers.3f:T7ea,实验分 attention-level、synthetic task-level 和 real workload 三层，而且作者做了 preregistration，提前写了 7 条可证伪 claim，这一点让结果更可信。

在 attention level，上述 certificate 的经验覆盖率达到 0.97，达到目标覆盖；certificate 与真实误差的相关性超过 0.94；同时没有带来精度损失。作者还专门测了 deterministic eviction 的自诊断信号失效：在真实任务上，类似 H2O、SnapKV 风格 eviction 的 retained-attention entropy 对 eviction-induced failure 的 AUC 约为 0.50，基本等于随机；一些其它在线信号如 margin 也接近 chance，evicted score mass 最多到 0.73，而随机化 certificate 可到 0.77–0.86。

在 synthetic long-context suites 上，certificate 能从 attention 误差转移到 task failure：16/16 个 model-task cell 都是正向 AUC，平均 0.836。这说明在压缩伤害主导的环境里，证书确实能反映任务层面的失败风险。

但真实工作负载的结果更克制，也更有信息量。作者明确承认 7 条预注册 claim 里有 3 条失败。原因是 LongBench 这类 question-aware eviction 在 25%–50% budget、6k 和 16k context 下本来就几乎不伤质量，所以总体 failure 更多来自任务本身难度，而不是 cache 压缩。于是 mean output log-probability 这种免费 baseline 在“预测答案会不会错”上反而优于 certificate；certificate-gated 从 25% 升到 50% budget 的 escalation 也没有收益。真正成立的是 attribution：在失败样本中，certificate 区分 eviction-induced failure 和 inherent failure 的 AUC 分别约 0.75 和 0.73，而 output confidence 在这个任务上接近或低于随机。进一步地，certificate-gated recomputation 在同等算力下优于 random gating 和 confidence gating；后者甚至可能低于随机，因为它把重算预算浪费在模型本来就答不出的样本上。整套证据链大约花了 70 GPU-hours，单 shard 在 H100/H200 上可跑。40:T70f,The work has two layers. First, an impossibility result. In a single-head, single-step attention setup, the authors formalize the online sigma-field available to the serving system: retained KV pairs, query history, scores, and any statistics computed from them. They prove that no estimator measurable with respect to this information can consistently estimate the true eviction-induced attention-output error under deterministic top-k-style selection. The proof is constructive: keep the retained state fixed, alter the evicted values, and the true error can change arbitrarily while every observable quantity remains unchanged.

Second, they restore identifiability via randomized design. The proposed mechanism is certainty-plus-Poisson eviction: high-score items are kept deterministically, while the tail is sampled with known inclusion probabilities π_i. Once the sampling design is known, design-based survey inference becomes available. The key implementation trick is elegant: Hájek correction is realized inside attention by adding log(1/π_i) to the logits of retained tail tokens, which performs inverse-probability reweighting through the softmax normalization. They then derive a retained-set variance estimator of Sen–Yates–Grundy type for the linearized error, and wrap it with an empirical-Bernstein radius to obtain a per-step error certificate. An e-process extension is also discussed to move toward time-uniform validity over the autoregressive trajectory.

Two aspects stand out. It is training-free and lightweight: no new parameters, no retraining, and only scalar work over the sampled tail. And its target is attribution rather than generic failure prediction: it aims to tell whether cache compression caused the damage, not whether the answer will be wrong for any reason.41:T84e,The empirical study is unusually disciplined: the authors pre-register seven falsifiable claims and report the failures openly.

At the attention level, the certificate achieves about 0.97 empirical coverage, certificate-error correlation exceeds 0.94, and there is no accuracy penalty relative to deterministic top-k baselines. They also directly measure the silent-failure phenomenon: retained-attention entropy for H2O- and SnapKV-style deterministic eviction gives AUC around 0.50 for predicting eviction-induced failures, essentially chance. Other online self-signals such as margin behave similarly; evicted score mass reaches at most 0.73, while the randomized certificate reaches roughly 0.77–0.86 on the same attribution-oriented yardstick.

On synthetic long-context tasks, the signal transfers to task level: all 16 model-task cells show positive certificate-failure AUC, with mean 0.836. This is the regime where compression damage is a dominant source of failure, so the certificate remains informative.

The real-workload results are more nuanced and more useful. Three of the seven pre-registered claims fail. On LongBench-style question-aware eviction at 25%–50% budgets and 6k/16k contexts, eviction is nearly free, so overall task failure is dominated by intrinsic task difficulty rather than cache damage. In that regime, mean output log-probability, a free baseline, beats the certificate at predicting whether the final answer is wrong. Certificate-gated escalation from 25% to 50% budget also does not help. What survives is attribution: among failed examples, the certificate separates eviction-induced from inherent failures with AUC about 0.75 and 0.73 at the two scales, whereas output confidence is at or below chance because it conflates task difficulty with cache damage. In recomputation scheduling, certificate-gated reruns outperform random and confidence-based gating at matched compute; confidence gating can even underperform random because it spends budget on examples the model would fail anyway. The full evidence chain reportedly costs about 70 GPU-hours on H100/H200-class hardware.42:T45c,For a skim, focus on three things. First, read the introduction and the theorem section to understand why deterministic eviction error is not merely hard to estimate but unidentifiable. That is the central idea. Second, inspect how the Hájek correction becomes a simple logit offset; this is the bridge from survey sampling theory to an implementable attention-layer mechanism. Third, read the figures and real-workload sections that separate prediction from attribution. The paper is strongest when it shows that output confidence is better for generic failure prediction, while the certificate is uniquely useful for diagnosing compression-induced damage.

If time is limited, the introduction, Section 3, the attention-level experiments, and the recomputation scheduling results are enough to capture the main contribution in 30–45 minutes. If reading more deeply, the variance-estimator derivation and the e-process extension are worth attention, especially if you care about extending the same randomized-diagnostic principle to token pruning, MoE routing diagnostics, or other online compression mechanisms.43:T45c,AdaDSF has three components. First, it runs a calibration set through the dense model and computes cosine similarity between each layer’s input and output hidden states. Layers with lower similarity are treated as stronger transformation layers and receive higher token retention ratios; layers with higher similarity receive less compute. The raw statistics are converted into bounded retention ratios through temperature-style normalization, a deviation control term with β=10, sigmoid mapping, and a global correction to match a target average retention budget. Second, each sparse layer adds a small MLP router that scores tokens and selects the Top-K tokens for full Transformer computation. Unselected tokens bypass the block through the residual path. Third, training aligns sparse and dense trajectories with intermediate hidden-state matching and output-distribution distillation. Compared with MoD-like or fixed-schedule depth sparsity, the main difference is that the compute allocation is derived from the pretrained model’s own layer statistics rather than imposed as a uniform or heuristic policy.44:T48e,PIVOT groups nearby queries and replaces multiple full-prefix scans with one shared scan. A group is aggregated into a single proxy query, which traverses the prefix once and selects a shared candidate set of size c. Then there are two variants. PIVOT-Refine rescoring: each query re-scores only the shared candidate set and picks its own top-k. This changes per-query work from O(L) to O(c), where k < c << L. PIVOT-Reuse is cheaper: it directly reuses the proxy top-k for all queries in the group, skipping per-query refinement. For a group of size g, indexing cost drops from O(gL) to O(L + gc) for Refine or O(L) for Reuse. The method relies on two empirical properties shown in the paper: high top-k overlap among nearby queries, and long-tailed indexer scores along the key axis, so a candidate budget only slightly above k is often enough. Importantly, PIVOT preserves the DSA interface and leaves the downstream Sparse MLA operator unchanged, making it a drop-in replacement. In prefill, groups are formed by contiguous query positions; in decode, the d+1 tokens from one multi-token prediction step form a natural group, so PIVOT composes with MTP speedups.45:T959,方法上最重要的是把“语义写入”从普通上下文利用中剥离出来。作者把 agent 历史表示成事件序列，一次 global prefill 后，每个事件的 KV 都已经被其前文上下文化。随后 serving 只取一个子集，故意删掉真正包含答案的 source event，只保留一个 downstream root event；这个 root event 的文本只引用 source，例如“ M mirrors S ”，但不显式说出值。若此时模型仍能回答 M 的状态，而且答案随 donor pair 中被删 source 的值切换，就说明 root 的 KV 行中已经 materialize 了上游状态。

论文围绕三个维度建立了“memory contract”。第一是 trigger：什么样的表面构造能触发写入。作者做了 16 种构造 bank，发现语义相近并不够，表面形式差异会让 write-through 从接近随机到 0.95 不等，说明 materialization 不是抽象语义层面自动成立，而是强依赖 checkpoint 对特定句式和关系模式的内部编码。第二是 landing：写入后的状态主要落在哪些被保留行里。结果显示 root event 承载主导 donor-aligned 信号，而某些 reference edge 更多像路由器，帮助查询回到 root；同时单个 row 的可读出内容还依赖 co-served 上下文，说明这不是一个完全局部、上下文无关的存储单元。第三是 access：这个通道能承载多大 payload。作者发现它更像紧凑状态通道，而不是通用信息通道：二元状态恢复明显高于随机，但 4-way、8-way 多分类接近机会水平，三位数字 payload 基本读不出来。

另一个关键贡献是“programmable carrier”。作者不满足于被动观察自然 mention，而是构造一种刻意书写、但不直接泄露答案的 carrier event，用来把上游状态写进后续表示。这个 carrier 能把 donor-aligned recovery 从 6% 提到 51%；在固定 query 位置上，只是把这个 carrier 与共享 downstream row 一起服务，就能把读出从 0.00 提到 0.42。这里的含义很直接：如果系统知道某类状态在未来可能需要、但原始操作数会被 eviction，那么可以在写时显式制造一个“承载事件”来提高后续可读性。不过作者也很克制，指出自然文本中的被动 harvesting 并不是可靠接口，真正工程上稳妥的做法仍然是保留显式 textual record 作为 fallback。46:T94f,The main methodological contribution is a clean causal probe for hidden state transfer through KV. The history is modeled as a sequence of events. After one global prefill, each event’s KV is contextualized by everything before it. Serving then keeps only a subset of event blocks, deliberately dropping the source event that contains the value of interest while retaining a downstream root event whose text refers to the source but does not restate the value. If the model can still answer the query and the answer flips with the omitted source value across donor pairs, the retained root KV has materialized upstream-derived state.

The paper organizes the phenomenon into a three-part contract: trigger, landing, and access. Trigger asks which surface constructions actually induce write-through. The authors build a 16-construction bank and show that semantic equivalence is not enough: constructions that are all easy to read can differ dramatically in whether they cause state to be written into downstream representations. This means materialization is sensitive to form, not just meaning, and must be calibrated per checkpoint. Landing asks where the donor-aligned signal resides once the source is gone. The dominant signal lands in the root event, while some served reference edges mostly help route the query back to that root. Importantly, what a row yields depends on what other spans are co-served with it, so the retained row is not a context-free storage cell. Access asks how much information this channel can carry. The answer is: only compact state. Binary payloads are recoverable well above chance, but larger discrete payloads collapse toward chance, and multi-digit values are absent.

A particularly useful part is the programmable carrier construction. Instead of passively harvesting naturally occurring mentions, the authors intentionally write an answer-free carrier event designed to commit upstream state into later representations without explicitly naming the value. This substantially improves donor-aligned recovery. The engineering message is concrete: if a system expects some state to be needed after its operands are evicted, it may be possible to write that state forward on purpose. But the paper is careful not to oversell this. Passive natural mentions are not a reliable interface, and explicit textual records remain the robust fallback.47:T743,The headline result is the donor-pair test on Qwen3-8B. Among donor-sensitive items, the model’s answer follows the omitted source value at a 99:0 ratio, even though no served span states which value is correct. That is the central evidence that retained KV rows can expose hidden upstream-derived state independently of visible text.

The programmable-carrier experiment is the most actionable systems result. On Qwen3-8B, an intentionally written answer-free carrier raises donor-aligned recovery from 6% to 51%. In a fixed query-position setup, adding the carrier alongside a shared downstream row moves the readout from 0.00 to 0.42. This shows that materialization is not merely an accidental property of one token position; it can be strengthened by writing a better downstream carrier.

The trigger study uses a 16-construction bank. Average read correctness of the constructions is reported at 0.98, but write-through ranges from chance to 0.95, and no construction is consistently strong across all three recent models tested. This is an important negative result: understanding a relation in text does not imply that the model will commit the resulting state into later KV in a way that survives source eviction.

The access-boundary experiments are also informative. Binary state recovers at 0.934 versus a 0.5 chance baseline, but 4-way and 8-way payloads sit near chance, and three-digit payloads are effectively absent. That sharply limits the interpretation of the phenomenon: it is a compact-state channel, not a general-purpose hidden memory bus.

Additional analyses on landing and co-serving show that the root event carries the dominant donor-aligned signal, while reference edges mostly help access it. The recoverability of a row also depends on which other spans are served together, which matters directly for eviction policy design.48:T5f5,Start with the setup, not the claims. Read the introduction and Fig. 1 carefully until the donor-pair comparison is fully clear. The key object is the independently served KV block of a downstream event, not the visible text span itself. Then read Section 3, where the 99:0 result is established and the paper explains how it avoids confounds such as explicit answer leakage, priors, and decoy elimination. The note about independently sampled decoys is worth attention because many memory-style evaluations quietly fail there.

After that, Sections 4 to 6 are the core. Section 4 is about trigger sensitivity and is the fastest way to understand why this is not a stable semantic API. Section 5 is the most relevant part for systems and memory-policy work because it studies where the signal lands and how co-serving changes what can be read out. Section 6 gives the capacity boundary, which is essential if you want to judge whether the mechanism is practically usable.

If time is limited, read the figures and conclusion paragraphs of Sections 3–6 first, then return to the methodological details. Section 7 is the engineering takeaway: programmable carriers versus passive harvesting. Appendix F is worth a quick pass because it explains why “dropping the source causes no loss” is not evidence that the source was unnecessary. A useful skim takes about 30–45 minutes; if you work on KV memory, long-horizon agents, or cache eviction, the donor-pair design and the access-boundary analysis deserve a closer read.49:T4ec,1) Estimation framing: each cached item x has latent utility u(x), roughly how much keeping it reduces future loss; an eviction policy is an estimator û(x).
2) Commit lag H as the key degree of freedom:
- H=0 covers existing approaches that decide at arrival: filtering (past-only signals like recency or accumulated attention) and prediction (learned guesses about future reuse).
- H→∞ corresponds to Belady’s offline optimum.
3) Fixed-lag smoothing: delay the keep/evict commitment by H steps so near-future evidence of reuse is observed rather than predicted, trading off buffer memory and latency.
4) Belady bridge via demonstrated utility: since neural attention lacks an explicit request stream, the paper defines a proxy “request” signal from which cached items were actually used by attention in correct near-future predictions.
5) Resulting policy: RMM, a training-free eviction rule that strictly generalizes H2O; additionally, a small model is trained to predict an ordering that is then measured/confirmed under the lag.
6) Regime map: when reuse is endogenous and temporally separated, smoothing can help; for common single-shot long-context reading, the measurement collapses to accumulated attention, making RMM effectively H2O-like.4a:T843,方法分三层：
1）训练层：不再训练一个通用 drafter，而是按负载分布做专门化。MTP（multi-token prediction）drafter 用更“对话/开放域”的高熵数据强化，追求短深度下的稳定接受；block-parallel diffusion drafter 用代码/数学样本强化，追求长可预测 span 的高接受与高摊销。这里的关键不是简单换数据集，而是把“接受率随深度衰减的形状”当作训练目标的隐含约束：高熵任务深度收益递减，低熵任务深度收益更线性。
2）架构层：提出 DFly，基于 DFlash 的 block-diffusion drafter 做两点改造：
  - Hybrid target-conditioning backbone：同时提供“全局变换后的 target 上下文”与“逐层（layer-specific）的 target 视图”。动机是不同 draft 层需要不同粒度/不同语义层次的 target 特征，避免所有层共享同一份固定表示导致利用不足。
  - Predecessor-conditioned autoregressive head：并行 backbone 仍一次性产出块内各位置的表示，但在输出头上用前一位置已选 token 做条件化修正，把位置边缘分布（marginal）拉回到前缀条件分布（prefix-conditioned），提升块内依赖建模与 suffix coherence，同时保留并行主干的吞吐优势。
3）推理/系统层：D-cut 把“验证更多 token”视为共享的 batch 资源。在线根据：a）不同请求当前前缀的期望接受收益（可理解为多验证一位能带来多少期望前进步长），b）profile 得到的 runtime cost model（并发、并行策略、硬件、目标模型结构导致的边际验证成本变化），在并发请求间重新分配验证深度：资源充裕时保留更长 draft，资源紧张时更激进裁剪低价值 suffix。
配套工程：AngelSpec 训练框架把 target hidden states 的生成与训练解耦（推理引擎流式产出 hidden states 给训练 worker），支持 MTP 的 on-policy TTT rollout、长上下文训练、以及 DFly 的逐层 target-conditioning 与可插拔 AR head，并提供在训 acceptance 评测服务，避免只看离线 loss。4b:T60c,Three layers:
1) Training specialization: instead of one universal drafter trained on an averaged mixture, train an MTP drafter on diverse conversation-heavy data (optimize short-depth acceptance under high entropy) and a block-parallel diffusion drafter on code/math-heavy data (optimize long-span acceptance where structure is tight).
2) DFly architecture (building on DFlash):
  - Hybrid target-conditioning backbone: combines a globally transformed target context with layer-specific target views, so different draft layers can consume target features at appropriate abstraction levels.
  - Predecessor-conditioned autoregressive head: keeps a single-pass parallel backbone but conditions each position’s output on the previously selected token, converting per-position marginals into prefix-conditioned predictions to improve intra-block dependency and suffix coherence.
3) Serving-time adaptation (D-cut): treats target verification as a shared batch-level resource. It dynamically chooses/prunes verification depth per request based on (i) expected acceptance utility and (ii) a profiled runtime cost model that captures concurrency, parallelism strategy, model architecture, and hardware effects.

At the fact level, assistant text KV can substitute for visual KV when the fact has been stated, while unstated visual facts are not reliably recoverable.4d:T4ea,Glide is a guided, layerwise non-uniform hybrid attention scheme combining sliding-window softmax attention with a linear recurrent aggregation path.

Motivation via measurement:
- They sweep softmax-to-linear ratios across layers and observe strong depth dependence: early layers suffer large accuracy drops when linearized; deeper layers tolerate linearization.

Mechanism:
- Partition layers into early / middle / late stages.
- Early: full softmax (δ = 0).
- Late: full linearization (δ = w).
- Middle: partial linearization parameterized as δ = α·w with a single scalar α ∈ [0, 1].

Key design choice:
- Reduce a high-dimensional per-layer configuration problem to a 1D knob (α), making the search/tuning and deployment much easier.
- Designed to integrate with existing retention-based hybrid architectures (e.g., Liger, LoLCats), rather than requiring a fully new model from scratch.

Difference vs prior work:
- Uniform hybrid methods apply the same policy across layers; Glide allocates softmax budget where it matters (early layers) and linearizes where redundancy is higher (late layers).
- Unlike pure sliding-window eviction, it retains a global information pathway via linear recurrent aggregation, trading exactness for lower KV cost.4e:T402,For LLM foundation-model researchers, the value here is conceptual clarity rather than a new decoding algorithm. First, it gives a cleaner lens for evaluating lossy speculative decoding: speedups are not close to free, and quality preservation can be overstated if the baseline is chosen incorrectly. Second, it provides a practical taxonomy. If a method is truncation-based, it should be compared against the target model using the same truncation sampling rule, not against the original target decoding setup. If it is collaborative, the key variable is how it handles overshoot tokens rather than its average acceptance rate alone. Third, the paper connects serving-time degradation to a broader modeling issue: a small subset of over-amplified tokens can dominate failure modes. That observation is relevant beyond inference, including calibration, draft-target mismatch, and tail-behavior analysis in training. This is not a paradigm-shifting paper, but it is a useful corrective for a fast-moving line of inference work.4f:T658,The paper starts from standard lossless speculative decoding and asks a distributional question: after modifying the acceptance rule, what distribution is actually induced? Under that view, existing lossy methods collapse into two families.

The first is truncation-based verification. Methods such as typical acceptance in Medusa and SpecCascade accept a draft token if it lies in an allowed set defined by a truncation rule on the target distribution, such as eta-sampling or min-p sampling. The key point is that these methods are not approximating the original target distribution; they are approximating a truncated target sampling process. This leads to the paper’s main evaluation correction: the right baseline is the target model decoded with the same truncation rule, not the original target model under standard sampling.

The second is collaborative verification. The paper unifies lenience-based relaxation and CoS by showing that both interpolate between the draft distribution q and the target distribution p, differing mainly in whether the interpolation coefficient is fixed or adaptive. The more interesting claim is that good speed-quality trade-offs do not require sophisticated global interpolation. What matters most is suppressing overshoot tokens, where q(x) exceeds p(x) too aggressively. These tokens are argued to drive most low-quality generations, while the rest of the distribution matters much less.

So the contribution is not a new verifier, but a unifying distributional analysis, a cleaner categorization of prior methods, and a sharper account of where quality loss actually comes from.50:T6a9,The experimental section is designed to re-evaluate baselines and expose failure modes rather than to maximize raw speed numbers. The main findings are as follows.

First, much of the favorable picture for truncation-based verification comes from the truncation sampling rule itself, not from the verification mechanism being nearly lossless. When methods such as SpecCascade are compared against the true baseline, namely the target model decoded with the same truncation rule, the quality gap becomes visible and grows with task difficulty. The paper explicitly notes that Figure 1 shows this widening gap for harder tasks, which matters because harder tasks are closer to realistic deployment settings.

Second, the issue becomes more pronounced when these lossy verification schemes are integrated into stronger speculative systems such as EAGLE-3. This suggests that distributional distortion can accumulate more severely in aggressive multi-stage or high-acceptance setups.

Third, experiments on collaborative verification support a more specific principle: selectively controlling overshoot tokens is sufficient to preserve quality better than broad interpolation over the whole distribution. This aligns with recent findings that low-quality generations are often driven by a relatively small set of overshot tokens rather than by mild global mismatch.

The provided full text excerpt does not include the detailed tables with exact model sizes, benchmark scores, or wall-clock speedups, so it would be unsafe to invent precise numbers. What is clear is that the paper includes baseline-corrected comparisons, difficulty-stratified evaluations, and integration tests inside EAGLE-3-style systems.51:T67a,The work has a diagnosis phase and a repair phase. In diagnosis, the authors build an end-to-end FP4 RL pipeline using HiFloat4 (HiF4), and compare against MXFP4 to check whether the conclusions are format-specific. They systematically vary precision assignments across rollout and training: low-precision rollout with higher-precision training, higher-precision rollout with low-precision training, and fully FP4 on both sides. A striking result is that restoring the training policy to higher precision while keeping rollout in FP4 performs worse than the full-FP4 baseline. This shows that the main issue is not training-side numerical noise but mismatch between the rollout distribution and the training distribution induced by quantized rollout. Activation analysis then reveals the mechanism: a small number of outliers expand the scale so much that the bulk of activation values underflow to zero in FP4. Keeping rollout activations in higher precision recovers much of the lost accuracy, but sacrifices the throughput benefit of true FP4 GEMMs. In response, the paper proposes Rollout-ResQ, a residual quantization scheme for rollout activations. Instead of using static PTQ-style calibration, smoothing, clamping, or rotation methods, which assume stationary activation statistics, Rollout-ResQ separates outlier residuals from the main activation tensor and represents them as a second FP4 tensor. This preserves low-precision matmul efficiency while retaining information that would otherwise be lost to underflow. The design is tailored to RL, where activation statistics drift as the policy changes and offline calibration quickly becomes stale.52:T710,The benchmark has two tracks. In the Data Construction Track, a method starts from raw domain sources and outputs supervised fine-tuning data. The resulting dataset is then used to fine-tune a shared base model jointly with Dolly-15k, and the adapted model is evaluated on held-out domain benchmarks. This design serves two purposes: it removes confounds from changing base models or training recipes, and it reflects a realistic setup where generic instruction-following data is supplemented with domain-specific supervision. The released baseline, Data-Construction-Skill, is a skill-guided agent rather than a one-shot prompt. It decomposes construction into reusable components such as output schemas, filtering rules, coverage constraints, and validation utilities. The point is not the agent wrapper itself, but the explicit structuring of the data-generation pipeline to reduce uncontrolled drift in format and quality.

In the Data Quality Evaluation Track, the input is a pool of candidate training datasets. A scoring function assigns each dataset a scalar score, and the benchmark measures how well those scores linearly predict the actual downstream performance of models fine-tuned on the same datasets. The authors release both the candidate pools and the ground-truth performance records, which makes offline comparison possible. Their baseline metric is Distributional Alignment Score (DAS), a distribution-based evaluator built from Maximum Mean Discrepancy between a candidate dataset and a domain proxy. The underlying stance is clear: a data-quality metric is only useful if it predicts post-training utility reliably. A key strength of the benchmark is that it places construction and evaluation inside the same downstream-grounded protocol instead of treating them as separate problems.53:T5fa,Three findings stand out. - Key reframing: attribution should be judged at the knowledge/support level, not merely by output sensitivity. Under IW/ICL overlap, sensitivity is not identifiable: removing a supporting span may not change the output because the same fact is available in weights.
- Metrics to expose this confounding:
  - BCS (Base-model Context attribution Score): evaluate attribution using a base model intended to have less IW access to the target knowledge, creating a control condition.
  - CAC (Cross-model Attribution Consistency): measure how attribution changes across models with different IW knowledge states; large, systematic drift indicates the method is reacting to IW overlap rather than contextual support.
  - APS (Attribution Preservation Score): quantify whether supporting spans keep their attribution when IW availability changes.
  - SSP (Source Separation Precision): treat the task as explicit source separation (ICL vs IW) and measure precision directly.
- Dataset: WMDP-Cyber++ adds provenance-style ground truth labels over context segments (which spans are truly supporting vs irrelevant, and which are IW-overlapping), enabling systematic evaluation.

Search Decision-Making covers evidence sufficiency judgment, whether to invoke search, and how to decompose or reformulate a query. The benchmark construction uses document-grounded reverse engineering. It starts from high-quality real-world documents as complete evidential hindsight, then works backward to synthesize a natural query, answer, localized supporting evidence, and reasoning structure. CLEAN preserves only the benchmark-authorized information state. GOLD keeps the same qid, model, action channel, reference target, and scorer, but adds a controlled source that makes the correct target value available. SHAM preserves the same source structure and exposure opportunity as GOLD, while substituting a matched incorrect value. This is the key move: the paper does not merely ask whether the agent was exposed to a source, but whether success tracks the correctness of the supplied value under a matched intervention. Two contrasts are defined. Delta_GC measures the total score response when the correct target becomes available. Delta_GS measures the correct-versus-incorrect value substitution effect under the same exposure structure. The latter is the central provenance quantity because it isolates value dependence from generic source effects. The intervention is instantiated on four standardized surfaces: retrieval, tool, memory, and subagent messaging. 协议层面，作者提出七点规范，核心精神是三件事：compute 要按 actual NFE 对齐，stochasticity 要显式 sweep，指标要成组报告而不是挑一个最有利的。实验覆盖 12 个 open-weight MDLM，参数规模从 150M 到 8B，包含 dense、MoE 和 soft-masked 变体；任务包括 OpenWebText/LM1B 上的 unconditional generation、HumanEval 代码生成，以及 GSM8K、HellaSwag、BBH 的 log-likelihood 评测。后面三类任务被作者当作 sampling-invariant sanity check，用来确认某些结论不是纯采样噪声。
