首先是数据构建。作者从 Anthropic 2026 Constitution 中手工抽取 40 个 constitutional values，并配上定义文本。随后用 Sentence-BERT 对每个 value 做嵌入，计算其与其他 value 的平均余弦相似度，作为 centrality score。两个偏组织性的 value——helpfulness 和 principles hierarchy——因明显更外围，被排除出 curriculum unit selection，剩下 38 个 value。作者再用层次聚类把这些 value 分成四簇，并按平均 centrality 从高到低排序，得到 curriculum 条件下的教学顺序：从更核心的伦理价值，到身份/品格/福祉，再到操作安全与关系行为，最后到认识论完整性与诚实。这里的设计意图很明确：如果价值之间存在结构中心与边缘，那么先教中心、再教外围，可能更利于形成稳定表征。

其次是 2x2 因子设计。两个因素分别是 curriculum ordering 与 deliberative reasoning。也就是：是否按 centrality 导出的顺序组织内容，以及样本中是否包含显式价值推理。这样得到四个 constitutional midtraining 条件，再加一个 replay-only control。语料规模上，摘要给出总 constitutional corpus 为 394M tokens，其中 reasoning 版约 257.6M，no-reasoning 版约 136.8M。这个规模不算大到改变通用能力分布，但足以作为一个有针对性的 midtraining 注入。

第三是模型与训练位置。所有条件都从同一个 Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base 出发，这是一个 hybrid Mamba-2/attention 的 MoE 基座模型，总参数 120B、激活参数 12B，预训练约 25T tokens。作者把 constitutional 数据插入 midtraining，而不是混在后续 SFT 里；之后再接一个 value-neutral SFT 阶段，确保如果 CMT 条件优于 control，这个优势主要来自 midtraining 内容，而不是后续监督阶段重复灌输了相同价值。

第四是评测设计。作者不仅看标准 alignment benchmark，还看 self-generated 与 established benchmark 的组合，并覆盖 alignment under pressure、value conflict resolution、blackmail、emergent misalignment 等更接近 disposition 的场景；同时在三个阶段评估：midtraining 后、SFT 后、以及 benign fine-tuning 后。这样可以区分“即时行为变化”和“能否穿过后续训练仍保留”的差异。

从方法论上看，这篇文章最重要的不是某个数据模板，而是实验隔离做得比较到位：同一 base model、同一后续 value-neutral SFT、同一 benign fine-tuning，只改变 midtraining 内容与组织方式，因此更接近在问“midtraining 到底能不能塑形”。a3:T892,实验结论可以概括成三层。

第一层，constitutional midtraining 相比 replay-only control，确实带来更强的 alignment，而且这种提升不是只停留在 midtraining 刚结束时。作者在 post-midtraining、post-SFT、post-benign fine-tuning 三个阶段都做了评测，结论是优势能够延续到后续阶段，说明这不是一层很薄的行为补丁，而更像是对模型倾向的重新塑形。摘要里明确写到 gains are durable and generalizable，并且 survive post-training and benign fine-tuning。

第二层，真正驱动收益的是 content presence。也就是，只要 constitutional 内容在 midtraining 中出现，收益就已经相当显著；相比之下，curriculum ordering 和 deliberative reasoning 的额外增益更像二级效应。这个结论很重要，因为作者原本专门为这两个因素设计了结构化实验，结果却发现“有没有把价值内容放进去”比“怎么排顺序、是否显式写推理”更关键。这对数据工程的启发比对齐口号更实在。

第三层，收益具有一定 OOD 泛化，并且在压力场景下仍可观察。论文列出的评测包括 alignment under pressure、value conflict resolution、blackmail、emergent misalignment，这些都不是简单拒答率能概括的指标，而是在看模型是否形成了更稳定的价值取向。作者还开源了数据和一组 120B checkpoints，方便后续做 mechanistic analysis，这说明他们也把这项工作视为“行为倾向如何进入表征”的起点，而不只是 benchmark 提分。

从当前提供的全文片段里，缺少完整结果表，因此无法安全写出每个 benchmark 的精确分数、提升幅度、训练步数或 token replay 比例。可以确定的硬信息包括：模型是 120B total / 12B active，底座预训练约 25T tokens；constitutional corpus 总计 394M tokens，其中 reasoning 与 no-reasoning 两部分分别约 257.6M 和 136.8M；实验是 2x2 因子设计加 control，并在三个训练阶段做追踪评估。若精读原文，最该补的是各条件在不同 benchmark 上的绝对分数、方差、以及 benign fine-tuning 后保留率。a4:T930,The methodology is notable for trying to isolate the causal effect of midtraining from later alignment stages.

The data pipeline starts from Anthropic’s 2026 Constitution. The authors manually extract 40 constitutional values and pair each with definitional text. They embed each value using Sentence-BERT and compute a centrality score based on mean cosine similarity to all other values. Two organizational values, helpfulness and principles hierarchy, are treated as outliers for curriculum-unit selection and removed from that part of the design, leaving 38 values. These are clustered hierarchically into four groups, ordered by average centrality. This produces a curriculum from more central ethical values toward more peripheral categories such as operational safety and epistemic integrity. The motivation is straightforward: if constitutional values have an internal structure, a central-to-peripheral curriculum may shape representations differently from an unordered presentation.

The training design is a 2x2 factorial setup with two factors: curriculum ordering and deliberative reasoning. This yields four constitutional midtraining conditions, plus a replay-only control. The abstract states that the total constitutional corpus is 394M tokens, with a reasoning-rich version of about 257.6M tokens and a no-reasoning version of about 136.8M tokens.

All conditions start from the same base model, Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base, a hybrid Mamba-2/attention MoE model with 120B total parameters and 12B active parameters, pretrained on roughly 25T tokens. The constitutional intervention is inserted during midtraining, not folded into later SFT. After that, the authors apply a value-neutral SFT stage so that any downstream advantage can be attributed primarily to midtraining rather than repeated value injection during supervised tuning.

The evaluation setup is also carefully chosen. The paper tests not only standard alignment benchmarks but also self-generated and established suites covering alignment under pressure, value conflict resolution, blackmail, and emergent misalignment. Importantly, evaluation is performed at three stages: immediately after midtraining, after SFT, and after benign fine-tuning. That allows the paper to distinguish immediate behavioral effects from durable changes that survive later training.a5:T777,The experimental findings have three main layers.

First, constitutional midtraining consistently outperforms the replay-only control, and the advantage is not limited to the checkpoint right after midtraining. The gains remain visible after value-neutral SFT and after benign fine-tuning on an unrelated task. That is the core evidence that the intervention is not merely a thin post-hoc behavior patch.

Second, the dominant factor is content presence. Once constitutional content is included in midtraining, alignment improves substantially. By comparison, curriculum ordering and explicit deliberative reasoning appear to have smaller, secondary effects. This is one of the most useful takeaways in the paper because the study was explicitly designed to test those structural factors, yet the strongest signal comes from the presence of the value-bearing content itself.

Third, the gains generalize beyond narrow in-distribution settings. The evaluation suite includes pressure scenarios, value conflicts, blackmail, and emergent misalignment, which probe behavioral disposition more deeply than simple refusal metrics. The authors also release the data and matched 120B checkpoints, making the work useful for later mechanistic studies of how alignment-relevant content changes internal representations.

The hard facts that are visible are: a 120B total / 12B active base model, about 25T pretraining tokens, a 394M-token constitutional corpus, a 2x2 factorial design plus control, and evaluation at three stages including post-benign-fine-tuning durability checks. In a full read, the most important numbers to extract would be absolute benchmark scores, variance across conditions, and retention after benign fine-tuning.a6:T606,This one deserves a close read. Start with the introduction, focusing on how the paper links shallow post-training alignment, alignment elasticity, and midtraining as an intervention point. That framing matters because the paper’s contribution depends on whether the post-training confound is truly controlled.

Then go straight to the method section. Three parts deserve careful attention: how the constitutional values are extracted and filtered, how centrality and clustering define the curriculum, and how the 2x2 factorial design is combined with value-neutral SFT to isolate the effect of midtraining. That is the core experimental logic.

In the results, read along the training timeline rather than by benchmark: post-midtraining first, then post-SFT, then post-benign-fine-tuning. This makes it easier to see which gains are immediate and which are durable. After that, compare the main effects of content presence, curriculum, and reasoning, and check whether the paper reports uncertainty estimates or multiple seeds.

Two deeper questions are worth keeping in mind. Why does content presence matter more than reasoning format? And does midtraining change shallow response templates or deeper internal representations? The released checkpoints suggest that the latter question may become the more important one over time.

If you already know the midtraining and alignment literature, a serious read should take about 60 to 90 minutes. If you want to build on the setup, the method and results sections both merit detailed study.a7:T5f8,There are three technical layers. First, the paper defines a sequential game with a prompt distribution, a reference policy π_ref, and a reward function r. The agent chooses a policy π to maximize utility, while a monitor performs sequential hypothesis testing on observed outputs to decide whether they came from π_ref or from a modified policy. If the monitor detects deviation, the agent is stopped. Second, the equilibrium analysis shows that the agent’s Nash equilibrium strategy coincides with the optimizer of the standard KL-regularized RL objective, maximizing expected reward minus β times KL(π || π_ref). The key point is not to invent a new objective, but to derive the old one from a statistical detection game. The KL term is interpreted as the cost of remaining hard to distinguish from the reference policy. The equilibrium also identifies an optimal coefficient β*, determined by the reward function, prompt distribution, and reference policy, rather than by manual tuning. Using the closed-form optimizer of KL-regularized RL, π*(y|x) proportional to π_ref(y|x) exp(r(x,y)/β), the equilibrium condition reduces to a scalar condition on β. Third, the paper proposes a stochastic bisection algorithm that estimates β* to ε precision by solving O(log(1/ε)) RL subproblems. The analysis draws on fractional programming and sequential hypothesis testing. Compared with target-KL heuristics, the logic is reversed: define the optimal detectability boundary first, then solve for the corresponding β.a8:T642,The work has two parts. The first is budget forcing. Instead of modifying the model, the authors implement a custom LogitsProcessor that counts tokens inside the <think> ... </think> region and, once a budget B is reached, forces emission of </think> by masking all other logits to negative infinity. A subtle but important implementation detail is that the chat template already inserts <think>\n in the prompt, so the processor must start with thinking mode enabled; otherwise the token counter is misaligned. They evaluate budgets B in {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} plus an uncapped condition with a practical 10k token ceiling, and define the minimum sufficient budget B* as the smallest budget that reaches at least 95% of uncapped accuracy and stays there for all larger budgets.

The second part is mechanistic early detection. Using forward hooks, the authors capture hidden states at early checkpoints in the reasoning trajectory and train linear probes to predict whether the generation will eventually converge. The choice of linear probes is deliberate: it tests whether convergence information is already linearly accessible in the representation, without adding a powerful classifier that could obscure interpretation. They compare these probes against behavioral baselines built from surface-level signals such as logit entropy and repetition statistics. They sweep all 28 layers at token 150, then sweep nine token positions from 50 to 300. They also run a contamination check on post-cutoff AIME 2025 problems to argue that the convergence-correctness relation is not just memorization.a9:T50b,There are four results worth retaining. First, token-budget saturation happens early. On both GSM8K and MATH-500, 256 thinking tokens are enough to recover roughly 95% of uncapped accuracy, so the marginal value of longer reasoning is small beyond that point. Second, AIME shows a strongly bimodal pattern: about 56.5% of generations converge naturally and achieve 96.5% accuracy, while the remaining 43.5% fail to terminate even under large budgets. The authors estimate that roughly 40% of inference compute is wasted on such doomed generations. Third, problem difficulty explains only a small part of the non-convergence phenomenon, with reported r^2 around 0.19, so this is not simply “harder problems need more thinking.” Fourth, activation probes beat behavioral baselines. In the layer sweep, layer 20 at token 150 is best with AUC 0.608 ± 0.080, and the strongest signal sits in upper-middle layers rather than near the output. In the checkpoint sweep, probes outperform behavioral baselines at 8 of 9 positions, with the largest early advantage at token 50, where ΔAUC = +0.074. The contamination analysis on AIME 2025 is also telling: converged generations are 100% correct while non-converged ones are 0% correct, reinforcing the link between convergence and answer quality.aa:T589,All main measurements use Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, a 48-layer model with residual width 5120. Behavior is measured with a two-axis judge: an answer is counted as broadly misaligned only if alignment is below 30 and coherence is at least 50. 第三步是因果检验。作者做的是 zero-ablation at full layer depth：在某层把目标 SAE feature 置零，然后观察目标 token logit 的变化，并沿完整剩余网络传播，而不是只看局部重构误差。对于跨 family 检测，作者指出 activation-based detection 在 LlamaScope 上会失效，因为 TopK 到 JumpReLU 的转换改变了激活分布，于是改用 decoder-alignment detection：直接计算 feature decoder 向量与词嵌入矩阵的余弦相似度，再施加同样的 gap/purity 条件。这样可以在没有激活数据时做跨 family 对齐。关键结论是：GemmaScope 和 BatchTopK 上匹配到的 single-token feature 更像“因果锚点”，消融后目标 token 排名常显著下降；而 LlamaScope 上很多匹配 feature 呈现局部冗余，目标 token 往往能很快恢复原排名，恢复率达到 96%–98%。作者还专门检查了激活函数差异，认为不能简单把这种差异归因于 TopK vs JumpReLU，本质上是 SAE family 学到的表示分解方式不同。ac:T7b4,实验规模是这篇文章比较扎实的部分。数据来自 6 个模型、3 个 SAE family，总计 3.9M feature，模型从 124M 的 GPT2-Small 到 9B 级 Gemma-2-9B，跨近两个数量级。主要结果有几组。

1. 单 token feature 的分布与几何：在 GPT2-Small 中，364/24,576 个 feature 被识别为 single-token，占 1.48%，其中 91% 位于 Layer 0。相较 polysemantic feature，这类 feature 在 decoder space 中聚类紧度高 4.7 倍，与 embedding 的对齐更强，文中给出 1.72 倍更高的 embedding alignment，显著性达到 p<1e-42。跨层持续性也更强，约为 polysemantic feature 的 2.7 倍，p<1e-73。

2. 因果必要性：在 7 个 model×SAE 配置、208 个 full-layer 条件下，178 个条件中对目标 token logit 的下降达到 Benjamini-Hochberg 校正后的显著水平。这说明 single-token feature 的“必要性”不是幻觉，至少在测量的 readout 上成立。但这种必要性随层深变化：早层消融更容易引发下游级联损伤，后层则更直接塑造输出 logit。

3. family 差异大于规模差异：在相近 8B–9B 规模下，LlamaScope 中检测到的 single-token feature prevalence 比 GemmaScope 低 46 倍。更关键的是，同一底模上的 token-matched 比较显示，GemmaScope 与 BatchTopK 的特征更稳定地承担因果角色，而 LlamaScope 特征在消融后 96%–98% 的情况下会恢复原先 token 排名，表现为局部可替代。作者据此认为 cross-family causal differences 超过 within-family scale effects。

4. 鲁棒性：single-token 检测阈值在 2 倍范围内变化时，定性结论保持稳定。因果实验还使用独立于激活统计的 decoder-alignment 方法，减少了“检测方法偏向某一 family”的疑问。

如果只看结果，最值得记住的不是“single-token feature 存在”，而是“它们存在且常常有因果作用，但这种作用不具备 family-invariant 性”。ad:T98d,The method has three main pieces. First, the paper defines single-token features using top-k activation statistics rather than relying on auto-generated explanations alone. For each feature, the authors compute Gap Ratio, Lexical Purity, and a Complete Word constraint over the top-20 activating tokens. They use a conservative operating point: gap >= 0.3, purity >= 0.6, and a full-word requirement. This captures only a small fraction of all features, but the choice is validated by explanation match, geometric clustering in decoder space, and downstream causal effects.

Second, the paper studies geometry and layer depth. It analyzes 3.9M SAE features from Neuronpedia across six base models and three SAE families: res-jb/GemmaScope-style JumpReLU SAEs, LlamaScope TopK SAEs, and community BatchTopK SAEs for matched-family comparisons on the same Gemma backbones. Single-token features are much tighter in decoder space, about 4.7x tighter than polysemantic features, and are heavily concentrated in early layers. In GPT2-Small, 91% of them are in layer 0; in Gemma they mostly appear in layers 0-4. The paper also reports a sharp structural transition from layer 0 to layer 1, with Grassmannian alignment around 0.26 there versus >0.9 for later adjacent layers. That suggests token-identity directions occupy a special regime near the input side of the network.

Third, the paper runs causal tests with zero-ablation at full layer depth. A selected SAE feature is zeroed at a given layer, and the effect on the target token logit is measured after propagation through the rest of the model. For cross-family detection, the authors note that activation-based detection breaks on LlamaScope because TopK-to-JumpReLU conversion changes activation statistics. They therefore introduce decoder-alignment detection: match decoder vectors directly against the token embedding matrix using cosine similarity, then apply the same token-dominance criteria. This allows cross-family comparisons without activation traces. The central result is that GemmaScope and BatchTopK token features behave like causal anchors, while many LlamaScope-matched features are locally redundant and recover their pre-ablation token rank 96-98% of the time. The paper also checks whether this can be reduced to activation-function choice alone and argues that it cannot; the difference appears to come from the representation decomposition learned by the SAE family.ae:T786,The empirical scope is solid for this type of work: 3.9M features, six models, three SAE families, and model sizes ranging from GPT2-Small (124M) to Gemma-2-9B. The main findings are as follows.

1. Distribution and geometry of single-token features: in GPT2-Small, 364 out of 24,576 features are classified as single-token, or 1.48%, and 91% of those are in layer 0. Relative to polysemantic features, they are 4.7x tighter in decoder space and show stronger embedding alignment, reported as 1.72x higher with p < 1e-42. They also persist more strongly across layers, about 2.7x more than polysemantic features, with p < 1e-73.

2. Causal necessity: across seven model-by-SAE configurations and 208 full-layer conditions, 178 conditions show Benjamini-Hochberg-significant reductions in the target token logit after ablation. So the paper is not claiming that token features are merely geometric artifacts; many are causally necessary at the measured readout. Layer depth matters, though: early-layer ablations tend to create downstream cascades, while later-layer ablations more directly affect the output distribution.

3. Family effects exceed scale effects: at comparable 8B-9B scale, LlamaScope has 46x lower single-token feature prevalence than GemmaScope. More importantly, token-matched comparisons on the same base model show that GemmaScope and BatchTopK features are causally anchored, whereas LlamaScope features are often replaceable, with pre-ablation token rank recovering 96-98% of the time.

4. Robustness: the qualitative conclusions remain stable when detection thresholds vary over a 2x range. The causal analysis also uses a decoder-alignment method independent of activation statistics, which helps reduce family-specific detection bias.

The key takeaway from the experiments is not merely that single-token features exist, but that they can be causally real while still failing to be family-invariant.af:T521,For a skim-level read, focus on the problem framing, the feature definition, and the matched-family ablation results. The authors apply Logit Lens to track the layer-by-layer evolution of answer-option logits in MCQA prompts. For each sample, they cache hidden states from every transformer block in a single forward pass. At each layer, they take the hidden state at the answer position, apply the model’s final layer norm, project it through the unembedding matrix, and extract only the logits for the option-label tokens such as A/B/C/D. This yields a ranking trajectory across layers. HDL is then defined as the point beyond which the relative ranking of options remains stable.

That definition is stronger than simply checking whether top-1 stops changing. It captures whether the model’s internal preference structure has settled. The paper then tests whether this phenomenon is architecture-level rather than an artifact. It does so through cross-model and cross-dataset evaluation, LoRA before/after comparisons, varying the number of answer options, and changing label formats. The label-format result is important: alphabetic labels and Arabic numerals produce sharper HDLs than Roman numerals, which hints that tokenizer statistics and token geometry affect how clearly commitment can be read out.

Relative to prior work, the contribution is diagnostic rather than algorithmic. No learned exit policy is trained, and no layers are removed. The paper tries to measure committed inference as a naturally emerging property of standard transformers. The main caveat is also clear: the analysis depends on Logit Lens, whose faithfulness on intermediate layers is still debated, and the setup is restricted to single-token answer labels rather than open-ended generation.b3:T5a4,The study covers four model families—Qwen, Llama, Granite, and Mistral—on four MCQA benchmarks. The main empirical pattern is that a distinct HDL appears across models, and layerwise accuracy often jumps sharply around that layer before flattening. The headline number in the abstract is a gain of up to +0.61 accuracy for Qwen on CommonsenseQA at the HDL relative to earlier layers, after which performance remains largely stable. That supports the interpretation that later layers mostly reinforce rather than revise the decision.

The most informative ablations are threefold. First, label-format ablations show that A/B/C/D and 1/2/3/4 yield clearer decision boundaries than Roman numerals. This suggests that token identity, pretraining frequency, and tokenizer behavior matter for observability. Second, varying the number of options does not remove the HDL, which argues against the phenomenon being a quirk of four-way prompting. Third, LoRA fine-tuning leaves the HDL largely unchanged, supporting the claim that it is tied to model architecture more than to downstream adaptation.

For a pretraining-oriented reader, the most interesting patterns are not the exact benchmark numbers but two structural observations: ranking stabilization looks abrupt rather than gradual, and ranking freeze is not the same as confidence formation. Later layers may continue widening the logit gap even after the option order has stopped changing.b4:T435,This is a skim paper. First, the paper detects context anxiety from reasoning traces. Instead of simple keyword matching, it uses a panel of LLM judges to classify whether a trace semantically expresses claims like 'this exceeds my context window' or 'I cannot finish within token limits.' This lets the authors separate anxiety-driven failures from capability-driven failures and successful attempts. That distinction is central to the paper. Second, it measures token-use calibration. After producing an answer, the model is asked to estimate how many tokens were required to complete the solution. This estimate is compared with the true token count through a winsorized token ratio. Invisible reasoning is defined as consequential computation in internal representations during the forward pass without an interpretable trace in output tokens. The key control is that the same filler sequence is used for every problem, so it cannot encode information about a particular question or answer at the token level. In evaluation, few-shot examples include the question, an assistant-side filler span, and the ground-truth answer; the test query is also followed by an assistant-side filler prefill before the model generates the answer. These criteria make it less plausible that the effect comes from ordinary semantic prompting, and more plausible that model-specific representations and attention dynamics are being used. The tasks are short and verifiable: 4-digit multiplication, 5-to-7-step nested arithmetic, and counting distinct assigned variables in code snippets. 第四，关于合成数据。作者比较了 7 个开源模型上的 instructed answer-first prompting，以及 Turpin 等人式的 hint-induced rationalization。两者在各自构造数据上都能被内部检测到，但只有 hint-induced variant 能向人工标注数据迁移，而且迁移到的是 incorrect-answer regime，而不是它表面上更像的 correct-answer post-hoc regime。instructed rationalization 则对真实标注数据两个 regime 都不迁移。这对常见的“先合成一批不忠实 CoT 再训练/评测 detector”做法是直接提醒：合成分布可能学到的是错的东西。bd:T78e,The paper makes three methodological moves. First, it audits the label semantics of FaithCoT-Bench and finds a mismatch between the benchmark documentation and the released data for the four-way faithful_type codes. The authors verify the correct interpretation using three independent checks: the relation between stored parsed final answers and gold labels, consistency with the benchmark paper’s own per-model accuracy numbers, and consistency with the released per-trace metrics. This data-level correction is important because the later regime analysis depends on it.

Second, the paper implements four families of behavioral detectors and evaluates them against the human binary unfaithfulness labels, rather than against derived benchmark metrics such as soft_faithfulness. The authors explicitly show that correlating a detector with soft_faithfulness is close to circular, because soft_faithfulness is itself a detector-like score. They also include premise-graph structure signals and counterfactual interventions with validated premise extraction, aiming to cover a broad set of black-box detection strategies.

Third, the authors stratify the problem by answer correctness. This yields a correct-answer regime, where the task is mainly to distinguish faithful reasoning from post-hoc rationalization, and an incorrect-answer regime, where the task is to distinguish honest error from unfaithful error. They then add hidden-state linear probes to test whether internal representations contain decodable signals even when behavior does not, and they compare two synthetic unfaithfulness constructions—instructed answer-first rationalization and hint-induced rationalization—to see whether either transfers to the human-annotated benchmark. That transfer test is a strong design choice: the question is not whether synthetic traces are detectable in isolation, but whether they share structure with real unfaithfulness.be:T837,There are four main empirical results. First, answer correctness alone—an oracle diagnostic, not a deployable detector—achieves AUROC 0.696 against human-annotated unfaithfulness, outperforming every purpose-built behavioral detector. The paper further shows why: 69% of annotated unfaithfulness occurs on incorrect answers, so much of apparent detection performance is really accuracy prediction.

Second, after stratification, the task splits cleanly into two regimes. On the complete-feature subset, the correct-answer regime has n=363 examples. There, behavioral signals provide moderate separation between faithful reasoning and post-hoc rationalization, with AUROC around 0.63–0.67. The benchmark’s own step-removal metric even points in the wrong direction. The incorrect-answer regime has n=270 examples and contains most of the unfaithfulness; in this regime, none of the tested behavioral signals performs detectably above chance.

Third, internal and behavioral evidence diverge. Linear probes over hidden states can decode the incorrect-answer regime in Llama-3.1-8B, with nested held-out AUROC 0.67 and selection-corrected permutation p≤0.03. In Qwen-2.5-7B, probes decode the correct-answer regime with p=0.014. Crucially, probes trained on one regime do not transfer to the other. The paper therefore finds no shared positively aligned linear direction across regimes, suggesting that “unfaithfulness” is not a single phenomenon.

Fourth, on synthetic data, the authors compare instructed answer-first prompting across seven open models with hint-induced rationalization in the style of Turpin et al. Both are internally detectable on their own constructed traces, but only the hint-induced variant transfers to the human-annotated benchmark, and it transfers to the incorrect-answer regime rather than the superficially similar correct-answer post-hoc regime. Instructed rationalization transfers to neither regime. That is a direct caution against the common practice of training or evaluating detectors on synthetic unfaithful CoT distributions without checking transfer.bf:T42f,A good skim order is by argument structure, not by detector family. Next, using a controlled interpolation ladder that swaps architectural components one at a time from the linear surrogate to full attention, it localizes static rank failure to the input-conditioned bilinear form XKX^T used for attention score computation — not softmax, not rank constraints. Since the operator depends on input, static properties of kernel K cannot capture actual task capacity.
It then redefines intrinsic rank in an attention-native way: the minimum query-key kernel rank that solves the target task within the attention function class itself. It also proposes energy effective rank as a robust capacity measure for softmax attention, as it is insensitive to small singular value noise introduced by softmax.
Finally, it characterizes the predictability frontier: exact data-only recovery of r* is possible for linear QK attention (even at scale with unknown V), while only partial energy-rank predictability holds for softmax attention due to nonlinear inversion corruption.c6:T765,The main idea is to disentangle context-length effects from order effects. For each target position, the authors construct two reveal conditions. In the intact condition, the preceding context is revealed in its original order. In the scrambled baseline, the same revealed span is permuted, preserving the word inventory and much of the topical signal while destroying sequential arrangement. A pretrained autoregressive transformer then provides conditional probabilities, or equivalently token-level surprisal, for the target span. By extending the revealed boundary farther back, they measure the incremental predictive gain contributed by each distance range. The difference between intact and scrambled gains defines the order-specific marginal benefit, and its dependence on distance d is the CPF, P(d).

Several design choices matter. They measure incremental gain rather than only comparing full versus truncated context, which localizes contribution by distance. The baseline uses permutations of the true words rather than random replacements, so lexical content and topic recurrence are controlled as much as possible while order is removed. The LLM is treated as a probe of structure in natural language, not as the object of analysis. The paper also includes controls with random-token sequences, synthetic corpora, partial order corruption, and analyses of whether the effect is concentrated in a few anchor tokens or broadly distributed.

Relative to Shannon-style context-length studies or Hilberg-type arguments, the novelty is the counterfactual baseline. Earlier work measured the total value of longer context but could not separate lexical availability from arrangement. Mutual information studies pairwise dependence, not dependence on ordered configurations. The contribution here is therefore a measurement design for sequence arrangement as its own statistical object.c7:T523,The study covers ten written and spoken corpora spanning six language families. The headline result is that CPF follows an approximate power law, P(d) ∝ d^-α, over nearly two orders of magnitude in distance, with mean α = 1.04, standard deviation 0.15, and median r^2 = 0.96. The concentration of the exponent near 1 is central to the claim that this is a reproducible law rather than a loose curve fit.

The control experiments are important. The effect largely disappears on scrambled or random-token controls and on synthetic corpora, which argues against the pattern being a trivial artifact of the probe. When sequential integrity is progressively degraded, CPF weakens accordingly, supporting the interpretation that it is measuring order-specific signal rather than simple lexical recurrence. The paper also reports that the contribution is broadly distributed across prior sentences rather than being dominated by a few distant anchor tokens.

The experimental strength is not a model-size sweep or benchmark gains. It comes from replication across corpora and from careful controls that rule out obvious confounds. For a pretraining reader, the most informative parts are the ablations around the scrambled baseline, synthetic controls, partial corruption, and sentence-level contribution distribution.c8:T402,The method is a controlled adaptation benchmark spanning five objective types: lexical binding, factual association, behavioral policy learning, causal mapping, and procedural reasoning. For each objective, they measure three outcomes: whether the target behavior is acquired, whether it transfers to held-out contexts, and whether it stays bounded rather than over-applying. This yields an adaptation geometry for each learning type. The important idea is that LoRA is used here as a controlled intervention tool, not mainly as an efficiency method. That distinguishes the work from standard PEFT papers, which usually optimize parameter budget versus downstream accuracy, and from model-editing papers that focus mostly on factual memory. The paper broadens the scope to behavior, causality, and procedural structure, and asks whether layer location itself reveals something about the kind of learning being introduced.c9:T431,The main empirical finding is that the five objective classes exhibit distinct depth-wise signatures. Factual association prefers later layers among localized adaptations. Behavioral policy learning, causal mapping, and procedural reasoning show different preferences again, indicating that these are not interchangeable forms of adaptation. A key message is that localized adaptation is not merely a cheaper approximation to full fine-tuning. It changes the character of what is learned. Some sites support narrow acquisition but poor transfer; others encourage overgeneralization. The material provided here does not include the full numeric tables or model sizes, but the experimental structure is already clear: compare early/middle/late/full-stack LoRA and evaluate acquisition, transfer, and boundedness separately. Given a larger source MLLM and a smaller target MLLM from the same family, the model is partitioned into three components: vision encoder (ViT), cross-modal projector, and LLM. An injection space E=(C,P) specifies which components are selected and whether the injection is restricted to linear-layer parameters or extended to all alignable parameters. Because source and target differ in hidden size, attention-head count, and LLM depth, the paper defines a heterogeneous alignment operator A_pi that projects source parameters into the target parameter space. The layer mapping pi controls how source LLM layers are matched to target layers.

After obtaining the projected source direction Δ, the target is perturbed without training: Θ_F = Θ_T + αΔ. The point is not to perform aggressive fusion, but to scan α, parameter scope, component choice, and layer mapping, and then observe capability-specific local changes.

The theoretical analysis uses a second-order expansion around the target parameters. For a capability-specific loss L_c(Θ), the local gain is approximated by a first-order term αA_c minus a second-order term proportional to α^2 I_c, where A_c = -∇L_c(Θ_T)^TΔ is the transfer signal and I_c = Δ^T H_c Δ is the curvature response. This decomposition is the conceptual center of the paper. It explains why the same injected direction can help reasoning but barely affect perception, and why gains vanish once α becomes too large: the first-order alignment may be positive, but structural interference grows quadratically.

Unlike standard model merging, the method is not trying to build the best merged model, and it does not rely on learned mappings. It is a controlled probe for transferability. One notable design choice is the comparison between linear-only and full-parameter injection. The results suggest that transferable knowledge is more concentrated in linear transformations than in the full set of alignable weights, which is an interesting clue about where portable computation lives in MLLMs.cc:T6ad,The experiments use four Qwen3-VL cross-scale model pairs and evaluate them on twelve benchmarks. The most informative results are capability-wise rather than aggregate.

First, gains are concentrated in reasoning, especially high-level reasoning, while perception remains close to the original target performance. This suggests that training-free cross-scale fusion is much better at transferring high-level decision or language-side computation than low-level visual competence.

Second, component-level ablations show that the LLM carries most of the high-level reasoning gains. Injecting the ViT or projector does not produce comparable positive transfer. This is consistent with the idea that visual capability is more tightly coupled to representation geometry and encoder-specific details, making it less amenable to local linear projection.

Third, restricting injection to linear-layer parameters is usually more efficient and more stable than injecting all alignable parameters. Full-parameter injection may contain more useful signal, but it also introduces substantially more structural conflict, which matches the second-order analysis.

Fourth, both layer mapping and injection ratio are highly sensitive. Effective layer mappings depend on the specific source-target pair; there is no universal best mapping. Positive selective transfer appears only in a narrow low-α regime, and performance degrades quickly as α increases, consistent with a linear benefit term competing against a quadratic interference term.

The most useful ablations are the capability breakdown, component-wise injection, linear-vs-full comparison, and α sweeps. Those are where the paper’s actual contribution sits.cd:T55d,Read it in three passes: setup, theory, then ablations.

In resample, the model sees only the original prompt again. In placebo, it sees its failed program plus a content-free notice that it was wrong. In feedback, it also receives the actual failing input, expected output, and observed output. In reflect, it is asked to diagnose the failure in prose before rewriting the code. This separates the value of another draw, self-exposure, diagnostic feedback, and verbal reflection. Retry attempts use temperature 0.8; the authors explicitly avoid greedy retry because it would return byte-identical programs and make resampling meaningless. Each trajectory allows up to k=8 attempts, and pass@1 for all k≤8 is read from the same trajectory. Paired contrasts are tested with exact McNemar tests, task-level bootstrap intervals, and Holm correction. First, reuse existing Python abstractions. In NOOA, a class defines the agent, fields hold explicit model-visible state, methods define capabilities, type annotations specify contracts, exceptions handle failures, and asyncio handles concurrency. Second, treat agentic loops as ordinary method calls. If a method has a normal body, it runs as deterministic Python; if the body is just an ellipsis (...), the runtime interprets it as an LLM-driven agentic method. That means the application sees a typed function call rather than an unstructured text exchange.

Third, deterministic work should be moved out of the agent loop. Parsing, arithmetic, state transitions, and rule-based logic should live in ordinary methods that the model can call. Fourth, leverage the model's existing Python knowledge. Instead of constraining the model to a narrow tool-calling DSL, NOOA allows CodeAct-style methods to write and execute ordinary Python using loops, conditionals, imports, libraries, async code, and external clients. Fifth, expose the harness through explicit APIs. Context construction, event history, and state rendering are not hidden framework internals; they are surfaced as Pythonic interfaces available to both developers and the model.

The central idea is to collapse several layers of agent specification into one class definition: source code, prompt surface, tool interface, state boundary, and type contract. The paper also emphasizes that inputs need not be serialized into text only; live Python objects and even images can be passed by reference, with the harness rendering bounded previews for the model while preserving executable object access for code paths.d1:T41f,The empirical section is mostly capability validation rather than training-oriented measurement. What is clear is that the authors are trying to show that the interface is usable on nontrivial agent tasks, not just toy examples.

There is also a framework comparison section covering fourteen other agent frameworks or harnesses against six interface capabilities. That comparison is meant to position NOOA as a more unified programming model, especially around typed contracts, state, prompt surface, and runtime extensibility. It is more of a design-space comparison than a strict benchmark.

So the right reading of the experiments is modest: they support feasibility and usability of the interface, but they do not establish a strong performance advantage over other agent paradigms.d2:T569,The method is State Transition Pretraining, or STP. Training data consists of step-level tuples (s_t, a_t, s_{t+1}), which can be extracted from existing trajectories or collected automatically from interactive environments. STP jointly optimizes two objectives. Forward dynamics predicts the next GUI state from the current state and action, effectively an image-text-to-image task. This is meant to build an internal model of how GUI states change under actions such as click, type, or scroll. Inverse dynamics predicts the action from consecutive screenshots, an image-image-to-text task. This forces the model to identify what changed, where the interaction occurred, and which visual details are action-relevant. A notable design choice is the use of a unified multimodal model rather than separate modules for perception, action classification, and state prediction. That allows both objectives to share a common tokenized interface and makes the pretrained model easier to transfer into downstream trajectory fine-tuning. The paper positions STP as initialization rather than replacement: it removes some of the burden from trajectory SFT by learning local structure first. The ablations suggest that forward and inverse dynamics provide complementary signals, and that the gains are not sensitive to whether transitions are sampled as full trajectories or as independent steps.d3:T40f,The main results cover both desktop and mobile GUI benchmarks. On AgentNetBench, under matched trajectory fine-tuning settings, STP improves average success rate by 2.3% to 6.2% and coordinate success rate by 1.6% to 6.8%, depending on the fine-tuning split. On AndroidControl, it improves step success rate by 0.9% and coordinate prediction accuracy by 1.3%. On GUIOdyssey, it improves step success rate by 0.6% and coordinate prediction accuracy by 1.6%. The paper also provides optimization evidence: the left panel of Figure 1 shows better cross-entropy behavior during downstream trajectory fine-tuning when initialized with STP. The scalability results are important. With fine-tuning data fixed, increasing transition-pretraining data steadily improves downstream performance. With STP fixed, scaling trajectory fine-tuning data from 2K to 18K still leaves STP ahead of the fine-tune-only baseline. That suggests the gains are not just due to extra data exposure, but to the structure of the forward and inverse dynamics objectives.d4:T506,The agent harness is decomposed into six discrete levers: prompt style (direct/structured/reflective), tool/retrieval policy (never/when_needed/always), memory policy (none/similar_successes/successes_and_failures), planning policy (none/brief_plan/plan_and_revise), verification policy (none/final_check/stepwise), and max steps (2/4/6), forming a total of 729 possible configurations. A DSPy-based assembler constructs the corresponding agent pipeline from a selected configuration. Two classic sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithms are used for online optimization: an ε-greedy contextual bandit (with linear value estimation and optimistic initialization to avoid cold-start issues) and REINFORCE (with softmax policy, linear-in-features logits, entropy regularization, and a moving-average baseline). A cross-domain verifiable task dataset, full training trajectory and reward decomposition logs, and a provider-agnostic deployment playbook are also released.d5:T440,WikiLoop represents external knowledge as an agent-native Wiki containing structured pages, inter-page links, and provenance to source passages. A Navigator searches, reads pages, follows links, accumulates evidence, and answers questions. A Builder proposes schema-constrained patches that create or revise pages, links, and provenance. Both roles are implemented by a shared role-conditioned policy, but with separate prompts, states, actions, and rewards. The training schedule starts with Joint SFT, then applies Navigator RL, Builder RL with a frozen Navigator evaluator, and finally Joint RL over role-homogeneous batches. The Navigator objective uses a sufficiency-before-efficiency rule: retrieval-cost pressure is applied only after evidence coverage is complete, reducing premature stopping. The Builder objective uses guarded utility differences. Each candidate edit is evaluated on affected queries and guard queries by comparing isolated before-and-after Wiki states under a frozen Navigator; affected queries measure target benefit, while guard queries penalize regressions.d6:T7c5,The core insight is to decompose the monolithic data mixture problem into two orthogonal sub-problems, supported by a closed-loop system with three modules: 1) Automated dataset-level assessment: Uses datasets as the minimal evaluation unit (aligns with industrial pipelines, avoids sample-level annotation noise) and adopts the LLM-as-Judge paradigm (Seed-1.6 model, 150 samples per dataset) to quantify three dimensions: capability classification (based on an extensible taxonomy defined via natural language, no manual labeling required, supports new capability categories), quality (4 dimensions, with hallucination penalty), and difficulty (6 dimensions, prioritizing cross-modal synthesis and prior knowledge requirements). Human alignment validation shows Spearman correlation r=0.82 for quality scores and r=0.75 for difficulty scores, meeting stability requirements for downstream optimization. 2) Decoupled mixture optimization: Inter-class ratios (token budget allocation across capability categories e.g., image-text vs video-text, grounding vs captioning) use coordinate-style single-variable iterative search, warm-started from the average of public reference recipes. Each round sweeps one category's ratio candidates while fixing others (with renormalization) and selects the value with best validation performance, avoiding multi-variable confounding. Intra-class ratios (e.g., mixing multiple OCR datasets) use constrained convex optimization, with an explicit entropy term in the objective to enforce diversity, weighted by quality and difficulty scores to avoid redundant stacking. 3) Standardized data admission: Fixes inter-class ratios, total token budget, and intra-class strategy, turning new dataset addition into a single-variable controlled intervention whose impact can be measured directly without full recipe re-sweeping. Multiple-Choice-Question (MCQ) validation is used to evaluate proxy checkpoints to reduce dependence on free-form instruction following.d7:T47d,Key reported results include: 1) Automated dataset-level high-dimensional joint search, with an interpretable and reproducible process. 3) Ratios searched on proxy-scale models transfer directly to larger model and data scales without additional tuning. 4) A VLM trained with 80B additional multimodal continued-pretraining tokens under the optimized recipe matches the performance of strong contemporary open-source baselines (LLaVA series, Qwen3-VL, Points for further exploration: how validation set selection for inter-class search avoids overfitting, integration of difficulty scores with data curriculum learning, and the boundary of entropy term weight's suppression effect on redundant data.d9:T74c,技术路线是一个端到端 CuraWeb curation framework。原始数据来自 2013–2024 年的 12 年 Common Crawl snapshots。先用 Resiliparse 从 WARC 抽取正文，去掉 header、footer 和广告噪声；再用 FastText 语言分类器保留 English confidence > 0.5 的文档；exact dedup 用全局 SHA-256 文档哈希；随后用扩展 URL blacklist 去掉 spam 和成人内容域。这个基础漏斗从 184.9B raw documents 压到 41.4B unique documents，保留率 22.4%；URL blacklist 后得到 39.1B documents，保留率 94.5%。

核心创新有三块。第一是 dual-track cleaning。规则过滤不再使用统一阈值，而是根据 domain 调整阈值，避免数学、代码等高价值领域因符号密度、长度分布或格式特征被误杀。模型驱动部分使用 data understanding model 给文档打多维标签，包括 writing quality、content value 和 domain tags。第二是 hybrid deduplication。传统 n-gram / LSH 能处理显性重复，但对两类 hidden redundancy 不够：一种是 templatized clusters，即页面结构高度相同但局部参数不同；另一种是 redundant crawling，即相似度刚好落在 LSH 阈值下方的重复抓取。CuraWeb 用 soft semantic deduplication 和 weighted voting：不是单条相似边超过阈值就删除，而是累计多个相似边的 penalty score，超过总阈值才判为冗余。这样比硬阈值更不容易误删边界样本。第三是 multi-objective sampling。writing quality 用 harmonic mean 聚合，因为任何一个严重缺陷都应显著拉低分数；content value 用线性求和，因为专业性、信息密度等维度可以累加贡献；再把质量指标与 diversity score 结合，保证 domain coverage。最终采用 Power Sampling，提高高信息量文档的抽样概率，同时不把分布完全压成单一高分区域。da:T7fa,The pipeline starts from twelve years of Common Crawl snapshots from 2013 to 2024. Main-body text is extracted from WARC files with Resiliparse, removing headers, footers, and advertisement noise. A FastText language classifier keeps English documents with confidence above 0.5. Global SHA-256 hashing performs exact document deduplication, reducing 184.9B raw documents to 41.4B unique documents, a 22.4% retention rate. An extended URL blacklist then removes spam and adult domains, leaving 39.1B documents with a 94.5% retention rate after that stage.

The main design has three components. First, dual-track cleaning combines domain-aware heuristic rules with model-driven document understanding. Instead of applying uniform thresholds, the rules are calibrated per domain so that math, code, and other structurally unusual but useful content are not removed simply because they violate generic web-text statistics. A data understanding model annotates documents with multi-aspect writing quality, content value, and domain tags. Second, hybrid deduplication combines n-gram-style filtering with semantic deduplication. The paper highlights two hard cases: templatized clusters, where pages share a structural skeleton but differ in local parameters, and redundant crawling cases that fall just below an LSH threshold. CuraWeb uses a soft semantic deduplication strategy based on weighted voting over multiple similarity edges. A document is removed only when its accumulated penalty exceeds a threshold, which reduces over-filtering compared with hard similarity cutoffs. Third, multi-objective sampling combines writing quality, content value, and diversity. Writing quality is aggregated with a harmonic mean to penalize severe defects on any single dimension. Content value is summed linearly to reward expertise and information density. A diversity score is added to preserve domain coverage, and Power Sampling increases the probability of selecting high-value documents without collapsing the sample into a narrow high-score slice.db:T714,JOLT follows the same high-level recipe as ToaST and ConvexTok—integer programming, LP relaxation, then rounding—but the formulation is specific to GL2R rather than split-tree or shortest-path inference. The model has two coupled sets of variables: token-selection variables indicating which candidate substrings enter the vocabulary, and segmentation-choice variables indicating which candidate segmentation is chosen for each pretoken. The objective minimizes frequency-weighted total token count.

The technical core is the greedy-consistency constraint. If a pretoken is assigned a particular segmentation, then at every segment start there must not exist a longer selected token that also matches the bytes at that position; otherwise GL2R would emit the longer token and the chosen segmentation would not be realizable. This is the mechanism that ties segmentation feasibility to vocabulary content.

A second important piece is scalability. A pretoken of length n has 2^(n-1) possible segmentations, so full enumeration is impossible. JOLT therefore works with a restricted candidate set and adds segmentations on demand, based on the optimization state, instead of instantiating the full combinatorial space. The corpus is first split into pretokens with a regex and aggregated by count; optimization is then run on the top-N most frequent pretokens. The LP solution is rounded to a fixed-size vocabulary, and the paper argues that rounding is not the main source of suboptimality because the rounded solutions stay extremely close to the LP bound. Relative to BPE, JOLT removes the dependence on local merge heuristics. Relative to UnigramLM, it is not a probabilistic latent-segmentation model. Relative to ConvexTok and ToaST, the feasibility constraints are driven by GL2R longest-match behavior.dc:T4d3,The experiments focus on compression, LP-bound diagnostics, and rounding loss rather than downstream language-model quality. The authors evaluate four training scopes with N in {100k, 200k, 300k, 400k} high-frequency pretokens. At equal vocabulary size, JOLT reduces held-out greedy-L2R token count by up to 0.78% relative to BPE, and larger scopes are consistently as good or better.

The more informative result is the lower-bound analysis. On the training scope, BPE is already only about 1%–2% above the LP lower bound, indicating that BPE is near-optimal for GL2R in this setting. JOLT closes 89.6%–99.4% of that gap, and the rounded vocabularies end up only 0.008%–0.176% above the LP bound. So the small margin over BPE is not a rounding artifact; it reflects genuinely limited headroom.

From a pretraining perspective, two caveats matter. First, the paper studies token-count compression, not LM perplexity or downstream accuracy, so the results should not be read as direct evidence of better model quality. Second, the setup is byte-level with single-byte fallback tokens, so there is no OOV issue; the conclusions are specifically about the compression ceiling of GL2R-aware vocabulary optimization under that regime.dd:T432,DataOrchestra combines an orchestrator with downstream tool models. Given a text chunk, the orchestrator first chooses among drop, untouch, and clean. For examples to be cleaned, it selects a subset of processing stages and generates example-specific instructions for LLM rewriting stages. The stages include noise pruning for line-level boilerplate and ads, surface rectification for formatting and grammar repairs, and pedagogical augmentation for math, Wikipedia-like, or reasoning-heavy content. Training uses a teacher LLM to propose initial plans, executes those plans with the actual tool models, and then evolves the plans using execution feedback. Stages that make minimal changes or harm the original content are removed; instructions are refined when the output loses information, introduces factual errors, or leaves residual noise. This produces 300K training pairs for fine-tuning the orchestrator. The important design choice is grounding the policy in the observed behavior of the tool models, rather than relying only on a teacher model’s high-level plan.de:T429,The paper proposes a five-level Data Pyramid: real-robot data, UMI-style data, egocentric and exocentric human interaction data, simulation data, and general vision-language data. The two primary axes are scalability and robot alignment. Real-robot data is directly aligned with the platform that produced it and has high physical fidelity, but it is expensive to collect and reset. UMI-style data removes the robot from the collection loop while retaining end-effector-centric manipulation signals, making it more scalable than robot demonstrations and more actionable than ordinary video. Human ego/exo video captures task structure, affordances, and hand-object interaction, but lacks robot-native action labels. Simulation provides controllable state-action trajectories, with transfer limited by assets, task coverage, and sim-to-real gaps. General vision-language data supplies broad semantic and perceptual priors but weak physical and action supervision. The paper further characterizes each source by quality, diversity, reusability, and physical fidelity.df:T5b9,1) Formalization:
- Define the set of valid tokenizations T(x) for a string x, including the canonical tokenization T_canon(x).
- Define tokenization invariance as identical model behavior for any t1,t2∈T(x), and quantify deviation via a distance d (performance gap or representation difference).

2) Non-canonical tokenization generation:
- Construct alternative token sequences composed of valid vocabulary tokens that decode to the exact same surface string, isolating distribution shift purely in token segmentation.

3) Evaluation protocol:
- A multilingual sweep over 27 languages spanning diverse scripts, 6 downstream tasks, and 3 recent model families.
- Importantly includes non-generation semantic tasks (e.g., cross-lingual sentence retrieval using embeddings), to test whether the effect is representational rather than just decoding fluency.

4) Mechanistic analysis:
- Emphasizes token fragmentation as a key explanatory factor: languages that are more fragmented under a shared multilingual vocabulary are more exposed to out-of-distribution segmentations; longer sequences and rarer subpieces can amplify sensitivity.

5) Training implication:
- Treat non-canonical tokenizations as augmentation: sample multiple valid segmentations for the same string during training to encourage invariance. Compared to swapping tokenizers and re-pretraining, this is a lower-cost robustness intervention that matches real-world tokenizer adaptation why loss spikes can appear when normalized networks are trained with strong weight decay. Prior explanations mostly emphasize learning-rate criticality, where the effective step size crosses a stability boundary. The paper adds a separate mechanism: weight-norm criticality. Normalization creates scale-invariant parameter blocks. Weight decay keeps shrinking their norms. As those norms approach zero, the local Hessian can grow rapidly even though the loss is insensitive to rescaling, and the optimizer can be pushed into an unstable regime.","importance":"The main value for pretraining research is diagnostic. Modern LLMs routinely combine LayerNorm or RMSNorm with decoupled weight decay, and loss spikes are often attributed to data batches, large learning rates, Adam dynamics, or global sharpness. This work shows that a particular normalized component can become unstable because its norm collapses, even when a global learning-rate story is incomplete. The contribution is not a new recipe, but a mechanism and a monitoring framework: stability can be checked at the level of scale-invariant blocks rather than only at the full-model level. It also clarifies why weight decay has a practical upper limit in normalized architectures: stronger regularization can improve generalization, but it can also move certain components past a norm-dependent critical boundary.","technical_approach":"$1b","experiments":"The empirical evidence spans several settings. The results indicate that neither normalization nor weight decay alone explains the spikes; the interaction is the driver. A synthetic regression setup further reproduces the chain from weight-norm shrinkage to Hessian growth and instability. A common challenge is the presence of straggling workers, which may significantly slow down training. Traditional gradient coding (GC) addresses this by duplicating dataset partitions across workers, allowing for the replacement of missing gradients from stragglers. However, GC requires workers to evaluate gradients on multiple dataset pa","starred":false,"priority":"p3","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-07-22T21:36:57Z","category_id":"llm_pretrain","cover_url":"/covers/2607_20739.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.IT","cs.LG"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作处理的是分布式训练里的经典瓶颈：straggler 会拖慢每一步的梯度聚合，而传统 gradient coding 虽然能容忍 straggler，却要求每个 worker 在每一步额外计算多个数据分片的梯度，常常把“抗拖尾”换成了“更高计算时延”。论文要解决的不是编码能不能恢复全梯度，而是如何在不增加单步计算负担的前提下，保留 gradient coding 的容错能力。","importance":"对大模型预训练的直接启发不在建模范式，而在训练系统层面的取舍：很多容错方法默认通信或恢复是主矛盾，但在真实训练里，额外前向/反向计算往往更贵。这篇论文给出的结论很明确：如果编码方案把每步计算量放大 c=s+1 倍，那么即便能少等 straggler，端到端 wall-clock 也可能更差。它的价值在于把“编码冗余”改写成“跨步流水化冗余”，这对大规模异构集群、低稳定性云资源、或弹性训练环境有参考意义。不过它离当前主流 LLM 训练栈还有距离，更多是系统思路上的启发，而不是可以直接照搬的 recipe。","technical_approach":"核心方法是 Pipelined Gradient Coding, PGC。思路很朴素但设计上不简单：传统 GC 在同一步里让每个 worker 计算 c 个分片梯度，再上传编码后的线性组合；PGC 则把这 c 份计算拆到连续多个 step 中，每个 worker 每一步只算 1 个分片，因此单步计算负担回到和普通 DGD 一样。为了仍然能恢复全局梯度，PGC 让当前 step 上传的 coded gradient 同时依赖当前和历史 step 已经算过的分片梯度，于是形成跨时间的流水线。\n\n论文分别为两类经典 placement 设计了 PGC：\n1. Fractional Repetition (FR)：worker 分组后共享相同数据放置。PGC-FR 的编码和恢复相对简单，利用组内冗余在不同 step 上逐步补齐各分片贡献。\n2. Cyclic Repetition (CR)：数据分片按循环方式放置，更灵活，不要求 c|n。PGC-CR 需要更复杂的线性编码与依赖 straggler pattern 的解码。\n\n方法上的关键点有三个。第一，计算与容错解耦：把原本同一步内的 c 倍计算展开到 c 个 step。第二，引入 pipeline delay，模型更新使用的是带时延的聚合梯度，因此论文需要重新分析收敛。第三，证明在光滑/强凸等设定下，PGC 仍可收敛，并给出与延迟相关的界。换句话说，它不是“免费容错”，而是用可分析的梯度时延去换取更低的单步完成时间。\n\n和已有 GC 相比，区别不在编码矩阵本身，而在时间维度的重排。GC 是空间冗余主导；PGC 是空间冗余加时间流水化。和普通异步 SGD 相比，PGC 不是简单接受 stale gradient，而是通过结构化编码让 master 仍能恢复目标聚合量，只是这个聚合量来自跨步计算。","experiments":"实验分两层。第一层是动机验证：作者在 12 台 Google Cloud VM 上训练 ResNet-18/CIFAR-10，一个 epoch 内比较 DGD、GC-FR、GC-CR。结果显示，虽然 GC 与 DGD 在每 step 的 loss 轨迹一致，因为都恢复了全梯度，但 GC 的 step time 明显更长，文中给出的结论是相对 DGD 超过 100%，且随着可容忍 straggler 数 s 增大，差距继续扩大；GC-FR 又快于 GC-CR，原因是编码复杂度更低。\n\n第二层是 PGC 的收益验证。论文通过仿真和真实实验比较 completion time 与收敛速度，结论是 PGC 在保持和 DGD 相近单步计算开销的同时，能比传统 GC 更有效地降低总训练时间，并在 wall-clock 维度上更快收敛。这里要注意，论文强调的是“按时间收敛更快”，不一定是“按 step 收敛更快”，因为 PGC 引入了延迟梯度。对读者更有价值的观察是：在 straggler 不算极端、但 GC 计算放大明显的区间，PGC 的优势最成立；如果系统瓶颈主要是通信而不是计算，收益可能会缩小。","reading_guide":"泛读建议控制在 20–30 分钟。先看 Introduction 和 Preliminary，抓住作者为什么认为传统 GC 在真实系统里常常不划算。然后重点看 Fig. 3，这张图基本把论文动机讲透了：GC 恢复了同样的梯度，却因为每步多算 c 个分片而更慢。\n\n接着看方法部分里 PGC 对 FR 和 CR 的构造，理解“每步只算一个分片，但跨步编码恢复”的机制即可，不必一开始就陷入全部符号。若时间有限，优先看 FR 版本，因为更直观。最后扫一眼收敛定理和实验部分，确认作者如何处理 pipeline delay，以及收益是在 step 维度还是 wall-clock 维度体现。\n\n值得深挖的点有两个：一是这种跨步编码在现代 data-parallel LLM 训练里如何与 gradient accumulation、pipeline parallel、elastic training 结合；二是当优化器不是简单 SGD，而是 AdamW 一类带状态优化器时，延迟梯度对训练动态的影响会不会更复杂。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper targets a practical systems issue in distributed training: stragglers slow down synchronous gradient aggregation, while classic gradient coding tolerates stragglers only by making each worker compute gradients on multiple data partitions per step. That extra computation can erase the benefit of straggler mitigation. A naive design would be blocked by expensive communication-topology reconstruction, transient memory amplification during parameter and optimizer-state migration, and scheduling thrashing under token-level latency variance. Given a fixed budget, it asks how to choose model size, token count, and the text-versus-multimodal data ratio. This is different from the dominant late-fusion VLM pipeline, where a pretrained LLM and a pretrained vision encoder are connected by a projection module and then continued on multimodal data. Late fusion is efficient, but it inherits an optimization asymmetry: language and vision representations are learned under different objectives and distributions. The paper asks whether a single Transformer trained from scratch on mixed multimodal inputs follows compute-optimal scaling laws, and whether the optimal allocation for language and multimodal objectives is aligned or in conflict.","importance":"The contribution is mainly a scaling framework for native multimodal pre-training, not another fixed VLM recipe. It provides evidence that the attainable loss of native multimodal training follows predictable compute laws, so the regime can be studied with the same discipline as text-only pre-training. The important finding is that language and multimodal objectives have different allocation behavior. The language allocation law is relatively invariant to data composition, while the multimodal allocation law is sensitive to the multimodal data ratio. This matters for real pre-training runs: a text-heavy mixture may be compute-efficient only at larger model sizes, and the right mixture depends on the target point on the language-multimodal Pareto frontier.","technical_approach":"The paper formulates pre-training loss as L(N,D) under the standard compute approximation C=6ND, where N is the number of active non-embedding parameters and D is the number of training tokens. It then estimates compute-optimal model size N_opt(C) and token count D_opt(C). The analysis is done separately for the text objective L_text and the multimodal objective L_mm, rather than collapsing everything into a single aggregate loss. Two estimators are used. IsoFLOP profiles compare different model/data allocations at the same compute level and identify the best allocation directly. Training-curve envelopes estimate the minimum achievable loss from the envelope of training trajectories. Their agreement is an important sanity check: the result is less likely to be an artifact of a chosen parametric fit. The paper further introduces the multimodal data ratio r and models how r changes both the compute law and the allocation exponents.","experiments":"The experiments vary model size, training tokens, and multimodal data ratio for Transformer-based native multimodal models trained from scratch. Smoothed training loss is used as the common proxy because robust multimodal validation metrics are not yet standardized and each token is approximately seen once during pre-training. The main empirical result is that both text and multimodal losses obey stable compute laws, while compute-optimal N and D follow power-law allocation rules. Data-mixture studies show that the text allocation law is fairly stable across mixtures, whereas the multimodal allocation law shifts substantially with the multimodal ratio. Downstream evaluations add two useful checks: native multimodal pre-training improves pure-text spatial reasoning, and the resulting models show multimodal in-context learning behavior. The central issue is the coupling between two roles of the learned exit distribution: it acts as the inference-time stopping rule, and it also weights the per-depth training losses. As a result, a halting gate does not only choose an exit state; it also shapes the recurrent trajectory from which exits are later selected.","importance":"The work is relevant to pretraining and inference-time compute scaling for recurrent or looped language models. Looped Transformers reuse a shared block over multiple iterations, so adaptive depth is a natural way to allocate more computation to harder inputs. The useful contribution here is the trajectory-readout decomposition. It shows that failures of learned halting should not be attributed only to weak gate architectures. The training objective itself can change the intermediate representations and make the stopping problem ill-posed.","technical_approach":"The paper formalizes a looped Transformer as a sequence of hidden states h1...hT produced by repeatedly applying a shared Transformer block Fθ. A PonderNet-style gate predicts a conditional halt probability e_t=σ(gφ(h_t)) at each recurrent depth, inducing an exit distribution q_t. At inference time, the model exits when the cumulative exit probability exceeds a threshold. During training, the same q_t is used to weight the cross-entropy losses at different depths, usually with a regularizer toward a target depth prior. This creates the coupling: the learned gate controls both supervision allocation and final readout. To separate these effects, the authors introduce fixed-prior depth supervision, where a fixed depth prior shapes the recurrent trajectory without learning an input-dependent halting policy. They then evaluate post-hoc readouts on the resulting trajectories, including confidence-based exits, linear gates, MLP gates, and forced-exit diagnostics.","experiments":"The experiments span controlled synthetic tasks and larger pretrained checkpoints. The main findings are consistent across settings. Fixed-prior depth supervision can produce difficulty-aware trajectories even without a learned input-dependent halting policy. Simple confidence-based readouts often match or outperform learned linear and MLP gates in compute-accuracy tradeoffs. Pretrained ponder gates in Ouro are not uniformly Pareto-optimal. Its main lesson is that non-autoregressive objectives expose the model to a broad distribution of conditional prediction difficulties, and that this distribution should be controlled rather than left implicit. The proposed change is small but useful: make CTMC coordinate updates depend on local context while preserving each token’s marginal unmasking probability over time. This shifts intermediate states toward easier, better-conditioned prediction problems without changing the data and noise endpoints. Two mechanisms follow from the formulation. The first is a context-weighted sampler that can be applied to pretrained DFM models without fine-tuning. The second is a scaled cross-entropy objective that reweights token-level training losses according to context. Compared with fixed-order or block-diffusion approaches, it keeps any-order generation and only biases the probability path toward more informative local contexts.","experiments":"The experiments cover text and molecule generation. The main implication for pretraining research is that useful long-range dependencies do not always require learned routers or complex gating; simple information-theoretic cues can be more robust than gradient-based mask learning at long context. The main caveat is that gzip runs on CPUs as a preprocessing-style step, so its integration cost into training/inference loops and its portability across tokenizers and modalities remain open.","technical_approach":"The input is split into fixed-size blocks (b=128 bytes by default). For each block, a gzip compression ratio r_i is computed using gzip level 1; higher r_i means the block is harder to compress and therefore more information-dense. Blocks are labeled as literal or redundant using the within-sequence mean ratio as a threshold, so the literal fraction adapts per input. The attention mask has three parts: (1) all literal blocks are connected to each other for long-range attention outside a local window; (2) adjacent blocks are always connected via a small local window (w=1, covering 256 bytes); (3) fixed-position global tokens used by BigBird/Longformer are removed entirely. 方法的真实机制讲清楚：它们到底改了什么分布、为什么有时看起来几乎不掉点、有时却会明显劣化，以及这些方法之间真正的差别是否像论文名字那样大。作者的结论很明确：不少方法表面形式不同，底层其实主要落在两类机制里——基于 truncation 的 verification，以及基于 draft/target 分布插值的 collaborative 格式对照，系统拆分不同精度配置：rollout 低精度 / training 高精度、rollout 高精度 / training 低精度、以及两边都 FP4。实验发现，一个反直觉现象是：把 training policy 恢复到更高精度、但保留 FP4 rollout，效果比全 FP4 还差。这说明主要问题不是训练侧数值噪声，而是 rollout The challenge is not generic quantization noise. In RL post-training, rollout and training are tightly coupled: rollout trajectories define the learning signal, so if rollout-side quantization distorts the sampled distribution, higher precision on the training side may not recover the damage. If the judge must be re-run for every sample and every rubric change, large-scale data production becomes expensive and hard to audit. Programmatic judges offer a different operating point: reusable, inspectable, editable decision logic for cases where the rubric can be partially expressed as code. The use of a committee is important because a single generated program usually has limited coverage and brittle logic. Second, the system calibrates program outputs on a held-out validation set, selects useful programs, and aggregates their decisions into a final preference verdict. This is not just majority voting, since different rubrics produce scores with different scales and noise levels. 把评测组织成双向对战的多轮博弈。每一轮由“出题方”生成三元组：问题 q、参考答案 a*、以及验证逻辑/依据 v*（以结构化格式提交）。随后由独立的三模型评审团做两阶段判定：\n1) 验证（validation）：对 {q,a*,v*} 做有效性投票，采用一票否决（任一 INVALID 即拒绝）。被拒绝的轮次直接判为出题方自伤（-1），避免用含糊/不可核验/自相矛盾的问题刷分。\n2) 评分（grading）：若通过验证，答题方只看到 q 输出回答 r；评审团将 r 与 a* 对比，多数票决定 CORRECT/WRONG。\n计分只在“问题通过验证且对手答错”时奖励出题方；对手答对则奖励答题方。每个模型对每个对手做双向比赛以消除角色偏置（asking vs answering）。论文还强调一个关键约束：模型无法稳定提出超出自身知识边界的问题，因为必须提供可被评审团认可的 gold answer 与验证依据；这使 peer-probing 更像“我确实掌握且能核验的点，你没掌握”，而不是纯粹的刁难或幻觉诱导。\n从实现上，框架把“动态出题”与“客观可核验”绑定在一起：严格验证门槛 + 自伤惩罚，抑制了开放式主观题与不可判定题；多评审减少单一 judge 偏差。输出侧不仅给总 Elo，也给按维度（如定量推理、代码、逻辑抽象等）的失败画像与出题策略差异（激进高风险 vs 校准保守）。","experiments":"论文做了 10 个前沿模型的循环赛：共 360 场 match、3,600 轮（每场 10 轮，且双向）。作者报告该规模的全自动评测墙钟时间约 100 分钟量级，强调其可作为低成本持续回归。结果层面给出：\n- 模型确实能发现并利用同侪弱点，但通常不能稳定提出“自己也不会”的超界问题（受 gold+validation 约束）。\n- 出题偏好集中在 Application、L2 New Knowledge Learning 三层，使研究者能更清楚地判断瓶颈是在视觉证据定位、上下文信息调用，还是对上下文中新规则/新结论的吸收。对预训练研究员来说，这种分解有助于反推训练目标和数据配比：如果模型 L0 强但 L2 测模型能否从上下文本身学到新规则、结论、任务语义或经验知识，而不是回退到已有先验。这个划分比传统 document QA 或 chart QA 更强调“上下文依赖性”，也比一般 long-context eval 更强调 failure localization。第二，数据来源是多源混合：一部分来自公开 benchmark 的转换，一部分是新构造的领域任务，例如近期医学论文结论推断、金融报告中的 的一致性问题。也就是说，这篇工作的重点不只是“凑一批多模态题”，而是把任务组织原则、数据筛选、评分协议和误差分析放在一起，形成一个可诊断的评测资产。","experiments":"实验覆盖 6 个多模态模型、共 3,443 个样本。文中给出的最重要结果是：当前系统在这个 benchmark 上整体表现仍然偏低，最佳 overall score 只有 Standard calibration metrics collapse errors into unsigned quantities, so they cannot tell whether a model systematically favors positive or negative outcomes. Natural forecasting questions also lack ground-truth probabilities. OptimismBench uses paired positive and negative framings of the same scenario, forcing the model’s own answers to serve as an internal consistency check.","importance":"The work is most relevant to evaluation and post-training signal quality. LLM judges, forecasting agents, reward models, and data filters all rely on model judgments that may carry a signed prior. The base-versus-chat comparison is especially useful: post-training can set or amplify the direction of this bias even when the architecture and pretraining are held fixed. That makes optimism or pessimism a property of the alignment stack, not just of scale.","technical_approach":"The benchmark is built around inverted pairs. For each scenario, the model is asked for the probability of a positive outcome and separately for the probability of the corresponding negative outcome. A coherent model should produce complementary estimates. The paper keeps the sign of the complement violation as a Skew score, rather than reducing it to an unsigned inconsistency measure. It also decomposes the bias into positive-axis and negative-axis deviations from a 50-point anchor, which separates classical optimism, pessimism, compound overclaim, and compound underclaim. The tracks cover explicit-base-rate sanity checks, naturalistic uncertainty, action-versus-inaction recommendations, and opportunity-versus-risk salience.","experiments":"The main evaluation uses 16 models from 8 providers, 60 inverted-pair scenarios, and 10 runs, with a multilingual extension over 10 languages. The cross-lingual analysis reports that inter-model variance is 4.7 times inter-language variance. s","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-05-29T20:33:35Z","category_id":"multimodal","cover_url":"/covers/2607_21617.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.AI","cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇论文研究的是一个很实际但常被忽略的问题：VLM 就是扰动后的文本，而不是原始干净文本，因此可以明确判断模型是在忠实转写，还是偷偷纠正。这个设计比直接在现成扫描文档上评测更干净，因为扰动位置、比例、类型都可控。\n\n扰动分三类。Scramble 保留首尾字符、打乱中间字符，用来测试模型是否依赖词形整体模式和语言先验；Random 用同脚本随机字符替换，测试强破坏下的鲁棒性；Visual 用视觉相似字符替换，测试视觉歧义与语言先验的竞争。英文和韩文按词处理，中文按 4 字窗口处理。作者在 8% 的 eligible words 或字符窗口上施加扰动，并保留原始版本作为对照。\n\n评测对象分三类：通用 VLM、OCR-specialized VLM、传统 OCR。这个分组很重要，因为它对应不同强度的语言先验。通用 VLM 经过大规模多模态与文本预训练，最容易“脑补”；OCR 专项模型经过文档抽取微调，语言先验被任务约束部分压制；传统 OCR 基本是字符级识别，没有强生成式 prior。作者用统一 prompt 让通用 VLM 自然输出，不额外强调“不要纠错”，避免把现象用指令压掉。\n\n除了整体误差统计，论文还对 Qwen3-VL-4B 做层间 probing，分析何时发生 rewriting。作者发现，当扰动词的内部表示仍靠近原始词编码时，模型更容易走向“改写”而非“照抄”。另一个细节是词长效应：短词更容易被语言模型先验覆盖，长词一旦偏离正常拼写，模型反而不容易自信地纠正。","experiments":"实验规模是 1,455 份单页文档，覆盖 EN/ZH/KO 三种脚本，评测 15 个系统。主结果很清楚：通用 VLM 在扰动下的 WER 退化最大，英文上可到 4.5 个百分点；OCR-specialized VLM 的退化约 0.2–2 个百分点；传统 OCR 小于 0.6 个百分点。这个差异基本支持作者的核心论点：语言先验越强，越容易在 imperfect text 上牺牲忠实性。\n\n另一个重要发现是非局部效应。即便只扰动约 5% 的词，通用 VLM 在未扰动部分上的错误也会比 clean baseline 高 5–10 倍。这说明 rewriting 不是局部字符识别失误，而是整页上下文建模被带偏，模型会在更大范围内重写文本。对统一文档模型来说，这个现象比单点 WER 更值得警惕。\n\n跨语言结果也有信息量。结论在英中韩都成立，但最伤的扰动类型因脚本不同而异，说明 rewriting 既受语言模型先验影响，也受书写系统和字符空间结构影响。中文没有 scramble，更多体现 visual/random quantizer，把连续特征离散化为生成侧可用的视觉 token；再训练一个 image decoder，用这些离散 token 做图像重建。这里一个关键取舍是：因为视觉编码器冻结，训练目标可以只用重建损失，不需要再做图文对齐。这和很多从头训练 UMM 的路线不同，后者往往要同时处理视觉表示学习、离散化和跨模态对齐，优化耦合更重。\n\n第二阶段是 Unified Multimodal Training。作者不是从纯 LLM 初始化，而是直接从预训练 VLM 初始化语言模型及其图文接口，让模型继承已有的 vision-language priors。理解任务仍走连续 token 路径，生成任务则把图像表示映射为离散 token 序列，由同一个 AR 解码器统一建模。这样做的直接好处是：理解能力不必迁就生成 tokenization，生成能力也不需要第二个视觉编码器。\n\n和已有路线相比，差异主要有三点。第一，区别于 Chameleon/Emu3/VILA-U 一类把理解和生成尽量压到统一离散 token 空间的方法，Argus-Unified保留了连续特征用于理解，因此更重视语义保真。第二，区别于 Janus 一类双视觉编码器设计，它坚持单编码器，优先控制参数量和训练成本。第三，区别于从 LLM It focuses on coarse object-level attributes such as identity, color, size, count, and weight, avoiding fine-grained details that vision encoders often discard. It then reconstructs counterfactual images from the final-layer image tokens of frozen MLLMs. If those reconstructions preserve the relevant attributes, the visual evidence is still present in the model representation. The second part studies utilization. The authors introduce WhatIfVis, where each question can be answered either from the image or from prior world knowledge. They adapt controllable context sensitivity to the visual setting, yielding CVCS: a one-dimensional steering subspace that modulates reliance on visual context. A practical detail is important: vanilla models produce too few strictly successful bidirectional examples to localize the steering direction reliably, so the direction is localized in SFT models and then transferred back to the corresponding vanilla models.","experiments":"The reported evidence has three parts. Third, CVCS directions found in SFT models transfer to vanilla models and improve controllability over visual-context reliance. The main experimental message is diagnostic rather than just a benchmark number: for coarse attributes, utilization failure is a separable and common error source. token 处于低熵、模型极其自信的区域，行为策略和目标策略之间哪怕只有很小的 train-inference gap，也会因为某些近零概率项而被放大成很大的 ratio；这种大值并不一定对应真实策略漂移，而更像数值上被放大的采样噪声。相反，在高熵区域，策略本来就不确定，较大的 ratio 更可能落在合理波动范围内。第二步，作者分析异步 RL 的 staleness 的跃升。作者认为这不是应被统一裁掉的“坏 off-policy”，而是异步训练天然引入的探索。第三步，在上述分析上提出 ESTR，Entropy-Scaled Trust Region。它不是用固定阈值判断 |δ_t| 是否过大，而是让每个 token 的允许边界随其熵自适应伸缩：低熵 token 采用更紧的 trust region，避免噪声放大进入梯度；高熵 token 采用更宽的 trust region，保留真实探索。论文强调 ESTR 不需要显式重建行为策略，也不依赖人为 magnitude bias。实现上，它是 token-level 的筛选/约束机制，可嵌入异步 RL 流程中，替代传统的统一 ratio clipping 或 hard masking。","experiments":"实验重点放在长时程 agentic 任务和复杂推理
